definition_zh: 自由主义的；开明的；慷慨的；宽松的；人文学科的
definition_en: open to different views, favouring political reform, generous in amount, not strict or literal, or relating to a broad education in the arts and sciences
core_image: 一个不被绳索束缚的人，伸手把东西分给别人
scene: 社区听证会上，一位议员支持为低收入家庭增建住房。 The liberal member spoke for more low-income housing and argued that the planning rules should be looser.
sceneCN: 这里 liberal 是「政治立场偏自由派、支持改革的」（第 2 个义项：政治上的自由主义）；句意：这位自由派议员支持为低收入家庭增建住房，并主张规划规则应当更宽松。图中可辨识物件：听证会标牌、麦克风、住房规划图、选民登记表。

pos.zh: 自由主义的；开明的；慷慨的；宽松的；人文教育的
自由主义者；自由派支持者

derivatives.zh: 慷慨地；大量地；开明地
自由主义
使自由化；放宽限制
不宽容的；反自由的

senses.title: Open to different views
senses.titleCN: 开明的：能容纳不同意见
senses.definition: willing to accept and tolerate behaviour or opinions different from one's own
senses.definitionCN: 愿意接受并容忍与自己不同的行为或观点
senses.example: Her parents were liberal about curfews, as long as she called home.
senses.exampleCN: 她父母对宵禁时间很开明，只要她打电话回家就行。
senses.why: The core is Latin liber 'free'. A liberal mind is not bound by a narrow rule or prejudice; it leaves room for what it did not expect.
senses.whyCN: 核心是拉丁语 liber“自由的”。开明的头脑不被狭窄的规矩或偏见捆住，会为意料之外的东西留出空间。

senses.title: Politically reform-minded
senses.definition: favouring social reform, individual rights and government action, often associated with the centre-left
senses.definitionCN: 支持社会改革、个人权利与政府作为，常与中左政治立场相关
senses.example: The liberal party lost its rural seats in the election.
senses.exampleCN: 自由派政党在选举中失去了乡村选区。
senses.why: In 19c politics liberal meant free from arbitrary rule and favouring constitutional government. The label later shifted toward social reform, and its meaning still varies by country.
senses.whyCN: 在 19 世纪政治中，liberal 指免于专断统治、支持宪政。这个标签后来偏向社会改革，其含义至今因国家而异。

senses.title: Generous in amount
senses.definition: given or existing in large amounts; more than enough
senses.definitionCN: 给予或存在的量大；足够而有余
senses.example: Add a liberal amount of olive oil before roasting.
senses.exampleCN: 烤之前加足量的橄榄油。
senses.why: Latin liberalis already meant 'generous, munificent'. The free man was expected to give freely, so the adjective moved from social status to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 liberalis 本就有“慷慨、大方”之义。自由人被认为应当大方给予，于是形容词从社会身份滑到了数量。

senses.title: Not strictly literal
senses.definition: not strictly literal or exact; allowing freedom in interpretation or wording
senses.definitionCN: 不严格依照字面或精确表述；在解释或措辞上留出自由
senses.example: The translator took a liberal reading of the poem's last line.
senses.exampleCN: 译者对诗的最后一行作了较自由的解读。
senses.why: Freedom applies to wording: a liberal translation or interpretation departs from the letter in order to keep the sense.
senses.whyCN: 自由落在措辞上：liberal translation 或 interpretation 离开字面，为的是保住意思。

senses.title: Of a broad education in the arts
senses.titleCN: 博雅教育的：人文学科的
senses.definition: relating to a broad education in humanities, social sciences and sciences rather than narrow technical training
senses.definitionCN: 与人文、社会科学和自然科学的广博教育有关，而非狭窄的技术训练
senses.example: He studied liberal arts before law school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在法学院之前读的是人文学科。
senses.why: artes liberales were the skills befitting a free citizen, as opposed to a slave or a tradesman. Liberal arts still names that ideal of a broad, non-vocational education.
senses.whyCN: artes liberales 是“配得上自由公民的技艺”，区别于奴隶或工匠的技能。liberal arts 至今指这种广博而非职业化的教育理想。

senses.title: Noun: a person of liberal views
senses.definition: a person who holds liberal political or social views
senses.definitionCN: 持自由派政治或社会观点的人
senses.example: The bill split the liberals in the senate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项议案让参议院里的自由派分裂了。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a countable noun by metonymy: a person is named by the position they hold. Politics is the usual setting for this use.
senses.whyCN: 形容词通过转喻变成可数名词：用一个人所持的立场来指这个人。这种用法通常出现在政治语境。

senses.title: Free-market economics
senses.titleCN: 经济上的自由市场主张
senses.definition: favouring free markets, private ownership and little state control, in the classical economic sense
senses.definitionCN: 在古典经济学意义上支持自由市场、私有制与较少的国家控制
senses.example: The party is liberal on trade but cautious on welfare.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在贸易上主张自由，在福利上却谨慎。
senses.why: Classical liberalism put economic freedom alongside political freedom. Note the trap: in US politics 'liberal' often means the opposite on economic policy, so the sense depends on context.
senses.whyCN: 古典自由主义把经济自由与政治自由并列。注意陷阱：在美国政治语境中，liberal 在经济政策上常指相反方向，因此词义要看上下文。

senses.title: Liberal with: giving freely
senses.definition: generous in giving something to other people, sometimes to the point of excess
senses.definitionCN: 在给予他人某物时很大方，有时到了过分的程度
senses.example: He was liberal with praise and stingy with details.
senses.exampleCN: 他夸人毫不吝啬，给细节却很小气。
senses.why: Here the quantity sense is directed at people. Liberal with praise means the giving hand opens wide; the same phrase can quietly criticize someone who gives too freely.
senses.whyCN: 这里数量义对准了人。liberal with praise 意味着给予的手张得很开；同一短语也可以暗含批评，指某人给得过头。

senses.title: Not strict: allowing latitude
senses.definition: not strictly enforced or tightly controlled; allowing freedom of action
senses.definitionCN: 不被严格执行或 tightly 控制；允许行动自由
senses.example: The school has a liberal policy on mobile phones.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校对手机的规定很宽松。
senses.why: The freedom is now built into an arrangement, not into a person's mind. A liberal policy leaves the margin wide, which is why the word can describe rules as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 这时自由被写进了安排本身，而不是某人的头脑。宽松的政策把余地留得很宽，因此这个词既能形容人，也能形容规则。

intro.en: Liberal comes from Latin liber 'free', not from liber 'book'. Its oldest English sense was 'generous, noble', and 'free' ran through both the social and the educational branches.
intro.cn: liberal 出自拉丁语 liber“自由的”，不是 liber“书”。它最早的英语义是“慷慨、高贵”，而“自由”贯穿了社会与教育这两条分支。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'generous, noble, free', especially of a person of high birth or a free citizen.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪中期的英语，意为“慷慨的、高贵的、自由的”，尤指出身高贵者或自由公民。

items.en: liberalis 'of a free person, noble, generous, munificent' is formed from liber 'free' plus -alis.
items.cn: liberalis“属于自由人的、高贵的、慷慨的”由 liber“自由的”加 -alis 构成。

items.en: liber 'free' and liber 'book' are two different nouns. Library comes from librarium 'bookcase', built on liber 'book / inner bark', so library is not a relative of liberal.
items.cn: liber“自由的”与 liber“书”是两个不同的名词。library 出自 librarium“书柜”，建在 liber“书／树内皮”上，因此 library 不是 liberal 的亲戚。

items.en: artes liberales were 'the arts befitting a free person', the broad curriculum of grammar, rhetoric, logic, arithmetic, geometry, music and astronomy. English liberal arts is a calque of that phrase.
items.cn: artes liberales 是“配得上自由人的技艺”，包括语法、修辞、逻辑、算术、几何、音乐与天文这一广博课程。英语 liberal arts 就是该短语的仿译。

items.en: liber is connected with PIE *leudh- 'free, grow' (some sources gloss it 'people'). This reconstruction is generally accepted rather than certain.
items.cn: liber 与原始印欧语 *leudh-“自由、成长”相联系（也有资料解作“人民”）。这一重构属于一般认为是，并非确证。

items.en: The political sense develops in the 19c around constitutional government and free trade. In 20c US English liberal came to mean social reform and state action, which is why the word can sound opposite in different countries. It is never related to licere 'be permitted' (license).
items.cn: 政治义在 19 世纪围绕宪政与自由贸易发展起来。到 20 世纪美国英语中，liberal 转指社会改革与国家作为，因此这个词在不同国家听起来可能相反。它与 licere“被允许”（license）从无关系。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the two different Latins: liber 'free' gives liberty, liberate and liberal, while liber 'book' gives library. The near-meaning group separates the political label from attitude and amount words.
note.cn: 形近组的关键是两个不同的拉丁词：liber“自由的”给出 liberty、liberate、liberal，而 liber“书”给出 library。近义组把政治标签与态度词、数量词分开。

entries.definition: freedom from control or restriction. It is the abstract noun of liber 'free', the same source as liberal.
entries.definitionCN: 免于控制或限制的自由。它是 liber“自由的”的抽象名词，与 liberal 同源。

entries.definition: to set someone free from control, prison or occupation. It is the verb from liberare, the same 'free' family.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人摆脱控制、监禁或占领。它出自 liberare，属于同一个“自由”词族。

entries.definition: a place where books are kept. It looks like liberal, but it comes from liber 'book / inner bark' through librarium, not from liber 'free'.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书的地方。它形似 liberal，却出自 liber“书／树内皮”经 librarium 演变，不是 liber“自由的”。

entries.definition: favouring reform or new ideas, often more activist than liberal. It is a political label, not a word for generosity or education.
entries.definitionCN: 支持改革或新观念的，通常比 liberal 更行动派。它是政治标签，不表示慷慨或教育。

entries.definition: willing to accept differences. It names the attitude itself and carries no political programme.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受差异的。它只指态度本身，不携带政治纲领。

entries.definition: giving much or containing much. It overlaps liberal in amount and giving, but has no political or educational sense.
entries.definitionCN: 给予很多或含量充足的。它在数量与给予义上与 liberal 重叠，但没有政治或教育义。

entries.definition: willing to consider new ideas. It is more personal and less ideological than liberal.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意考虑新观念的。它比 liberal 更个人化，意识形态色彩更弱。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: liber 'free' + -alis, with liberty, liberate and deliver in the same family. The look-alike library belongs to liber 'book' and must be kept apart.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：liber“自由的”+ -alis，同族有 liberty、liberate、deliver。形近的 library 属于 liber“书”，必须分开。

normal.en: liber 'free' is the stem: liberal, liberty, liberate and deliver all carry some form of 'freeing'.
normal.cn: liber“自由的”是词干：liberal、liberty、liberate、deliver 都带有某种“使自由”的意思。

normal.en: artes liberales were the skills of a free citizen, which is why liberal arts means a broad education rather than a political opinion.
normal.cn: artes liberales 是自由公民的技艺，所以 liberal arts 指广博教育，而不是政治观点。

normal.en: library comes from liber 'book', a different noun. A library is a book-place, not a freedom-place.
normal.cn: library 出自另一个名词 liber“书”。图书馆是放书的地方，不是放自由的地方。

normal.en: deliver is de- 'away' + liberare 'free': to deliver a parcel is to free it from your hands into someone else's.
normal.cn: deliver 是 de-“离开”+ liberare“使自由”：把包裹交付出去，就是让它离开你的手、到别人手里。

normal.en: liberal with praise uses the generosity branch, not the political one: the hand gives freely.
normal.cn: liberal with praise 走的是“慷慨”分支，不是政治分支：手在大方地给。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with no lock: a person can walk out, and because they can walk out, they can also leave room for others to walk in. Liberal is that unlocked gate, applied to minds, rules and money.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有锁的门：人能走出去，也正因为能走出去，才会给别人留出走进来的余地。liberal 就是这扇没锁的门，用在头脑、规则与金钱上。

abstract.en: Freedom can be spent in three directions: given away as generosity, kept open as tolerance, or written into a curriculum as the education of a free person.
abstract.cn: 自由可以花在三个方向：作为慷慨被给出去，作为宽容被留开，或作为自由人的教育被写进课程。

abstract.en: The same word can mean 'leave it loose' and 'give a lot'. Both are the image of a hand that does not close.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以指“放宽”，也可以指“给得多”。两者都是同一幅图：一只不握紧的手。

examples.en: A liberal education taught her to question her own assumptions.
examples.cn: 博雅教育教会她质疑自己的预设。

examples.en: Pour a liberal amount of sauce over the fish.
examples.cn: 在鱼上浇足量的酱汁。

examples.en: He is socially liberal but fiscally conservative.
examples.cn: 他在社会议题上开明，在财政上保守。

dict_mnemonic.text: “离不了”——离不了自由，凡事主张放开 → liberal 自由的、开明的

root: 拉丁语 liber“自由的”（不是 liber“书”）+ -alis，核心是“不受束缚的、像自由人那样给予”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of liberal, all variations on 'not bound': a mind not bound by prejudice, a politics of reform, a hand that gives widely, a reading not bound to the letter, an education for a free person, and rules left loose.
sensesIntro.cn: liberal 的九个义项都是“不受束缚”的变体：不被偏见捆住的头脑、改革的政治、给得宽的手、不囿于字面的解读、自由人的教育，以及留得很松的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unbound person, whose hand is free to give and whose mind is free to admit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个未被捆住的人，手可以自由给予，头脑可以自由接纳。

branches.en: OPEN AND LOOSE: the same freedom applied to a mind and to a set of rules.
branches.cn: 开明与宽松：同一种自由，用在头脑上，也用在规则上。

branches.en: POLITICS AND ECONOMY: the reform label, the person who wears it, and the free-market branch.
branches.cn: 政治与经济：改革标签、持标签的人，以及自由市场分支。

branches.en: GENEROSITY: abundance in amount, and the open hand that gives to people.
branches.cn: 慷慨：数量上的充足，以及向人张开的手。

branches.en: INTERPRETATION: freedom from the literal letter in reading and translation.
branches.cn: 解释：在阅读与翻译中摆脱字面的束缚。

branches.en: EDUCATION: artes liberales, the broad curriculum of a free person.
branches.cn: 教育：artes liberales，自由人的广博课程。

intro.en: Liberal takes ordinary English suffixes: -ly for the adverb, -ism for the system, -ize for the verb, and il- as a negative prefix before l.
intro.cn: liberal 接的是普通英语后缀：-ly 构成副词，-ism 构成主义，-ize 构成动词，il- 则在 l 前作否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family of liber 'free' includes liberty, liberate, deliver and libertine. Library belongs to the other liber, 'book', and is not part of this family.
latinIntro.cn: liber“自由的”这一拉丁词族包括 liberty、liberate、deliver、libertine。library 属于另一个 liber“书”，不在这个词族里。

items.meaning: generously, in large amounts, or in an open-minded way
items.meaningCN: 慷慨地；大量地；开明地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Apply the cream liberally to the burned area.
items.exampleCN: 在烫伤处大量涂抹药膏。

items.meaning: the political and economic doctrine of liberal ideas
items.meaningCN: 自由主义（-ism 构成主义、学说）
items.exampleCN: 古典自由主义支持自由贸易。

items.meaning: to make rules or systems less strict
items.meaningCN: 使自由化；放宽（-ize 表示“使……”）
items.example: The government liberalized the visa rules.

items.meaning: not tolerant of different views; opposed to liberal ideas
items.meaningCN: 不宽容的；反自由的（il- 是否定前缀）
items.example: The ban was criticized as illiberal.
items.exampleCN: 这项禁令被批评为不宽容。

items.example: The adjective sits at the centre of liberal and liberty.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是 liberal 与 liberty 的共同核心。

items.example: It carries the free adjective into English as liberal.
items.exampleCN: 它把“自由”这个形容词带进英语成为 liberal。

items.structure: suffix naming a system or movement
items.meaning: a body of doctrine or practice
items.example: It forms liberalism, the political doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 liberalism 这一政治学说。

items.example: It forms liberality, the quality of being generous or open.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 liberality，即慷慨或开明的品质。

items.example: The army liberated the city at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 军队在黎明时解放了这座城市。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 自由；免于控制（-tas 构成抽象名词，经法语入英语）

latinEntries.meaning: to set someone or something free
latinEntries.meaningCN: 解放；使自由（出自 liberare“使自由”）

latinEntries.meaning: to hand over, save, or set free; literally 'to free away'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 交付；解救；字面“使脱离而自由”（de- + liberare）

latinEntries.meaning: a person without moral restraint; originally a freed slave
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放荡者；原指被释放的奴隶（自由义走偏为“无约束”）

definition_zh: 饿死；挨饿；饿肚子；使挨饿
definition_en: to suffer or die because there is no food to eat, or to make someone do so
core_image: 空了很久的碗还摆在桌上——身体里没有一粒米进来
scene: 战乱中粮车被拦截，村庄接连断粮。 People in the village starved during the long winter blockade.
sceneCN: 这里 starve 是「饿死」（第 1 个义项：因缺少食物而死亡）；句意为村庄的人在漫长的冬季封锁中饿死了。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「饥饿；饿死」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「瘦弱挨饿的人」

senses.title: To die from lack of food
senses.definition: to die because there is no food to eat
senses.definitionCN: 因没有食物可吃而死亡
senses.example: Thousands of people starved after the harvest failed.
senses.exampleCN: 庄稼歉收后，成千上万的人饿死了。
senses.why: When the bowl stays empty long enough, the body itself gives out.
senses.whyCN: 碗空得足够久，身体本身就会耗尽，意象的尽头是死亡。

senses.title: To suffer great hunger
senses.definition: to feel extremely hungry or suffer from not having enough food
senses.definitionCN: 感到极度饥饿或长期吃不饱
senses.example: He missed lunch and claimed he was starving.
senses.exampleCN: 他没吃午饭，声称自己快饿死了。
senses.why: The same empty-bowl image, softened into everyday exaggeration.
senses.whyCN: 同一只空碗的画面被软化成日常夸张的说法。

senses.title: To deprive someone or something of food or resources
senses.definition: to prevent a person, animal, or organization from getting food or necessary resources
senses.definitionCN: 不给人、动物或组织提供食物或必要的资源
senses.example: The factory was starved of investment for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂多年得不到投资。
senses.why: Withholding the food is the active hand behind the empty bowl.
senses.whyCN: 那只空碗背后有主动扣住不给的手，意象延伸为刻意断供。

intro.en: Starve goes back to an Old English word that first meant simply to die, and narrowed to dying from hunger.
intro.cn: starve 源自古英语，最初泛指「死亡」，后来词义收窄为「饿死」。

items.en: A reconstructed root *sterban- meant to die or be stiff, related to the idea of the body going rigid.
items.cn: 重构词根 *sterban- 表示「死亡；僵硬」，与身体变僵的意象相关。

items.en: Steorfan meant simply to die, with no special link to hunger.
items.cn: 古英语 steorfan 仅表示「死亡」，与饥饿并无专门关联。

items.en: Sterven gradually shifted toward dying of hunger or cold, especially in northern dialects.
items.cn: 中古英语 sterven 逐渐偏向「饿死；冻死」，尤其在北方方言中。

items.en: The meaning settled on dying from lack of food, and the old general sense faded.
items.cn: 词义固定为「饿死」，原本泛指死亡的含义消退。

items.en: Colloquial starving for very hungry became common, and starve of extended the idea to resources.
items.cn: 口语中 starve 用于夸张地表示「饿极了」，starve of 又把意象延伸到资源匮乏。

note.en: Starve looks like the unrelated word star, and sits near other hunger words of different roots.
note.cn: starve 拼写上与不相关的 star 相近，义场上靠近词源不同的几个「饥饿」词。

entries.definition: a burning ball of gas in the sky, or a famous person
entries.definitionCN: 星星；明星；只是拼写与 starve 相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to look at something for a long time with wide eyes
entries.definitionCN: 凝视；盯着看；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: to begin doing something
entries.definitionCN: 开始；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: to make someone very hungry, now mostly literary

entries.definition: to want or need food, or to long for something strongly

normalIntro.en: Build memory on the real word family and the death-to-hunger shift.
normalIntro.cn: 利用真实的词族和「从死亡到饥饿」的词义收窄来记忆。

normal.en: Old English steorfan meant to die, so starve carries a shadow of death in its root.
normal.cn: 古英语 steorfan 意为死亡，词根里就带着死亡的影子。

normal.en: Starvation is the noun form, seen in phrases like starvation wages.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 starvation，常见搭配如 starvation wages（饿不死但也养不活人的工资）。

normal.en: The phrase starve to death separates the everyday sense from the literal one.
normal.cn: 短语 starve to death 把字面义与日常夸张义区分开来。

normal.en: Starving is how people say very hungry in casual speech.
normal.cn: 口语里说 I'm starving 就是「我饿死了」的夸张说法。

normal.en: Starve something of something means to cut off supply, not only food.
normal.cn: starve A of B 表示切断供应，对象不只是食物。

abstract.en: Picture an empty bowl on the table that no one refills, day after day.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上那只没人续添的空碗，一天天空着。

abstract.en: Feel the body slowly running out of fuel like a fire losing its last wood.
abstract.cn: 体会身体像缺柴的火慢慢熄灭一样耗尽能量。

abstract.en: See a factory wilting when money stops flowing, like a field with no rain.
abstract.cn: 看工厂在资金断流下枯萎，如同无雨的田地。

examples.en: The prisoners were starved and given almost no water.
examples.cn: 囚犯们被断食，几乎不给水。

examples.en: I skipped breakfast and I'm absolutely starving now.
examples.cn: 我没吃早饭，现在饿得不行。

examples.en: The research lab was starved of funding for two years.
examples.cn: 这家研究实验室两年缺乏经费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死他饿夫」——一家老小没饭吃，最后「死他饿」倒下的画面，帮助记住饿死之意。

root: 一般认为源自日耳曼语词根 *sterban-（死亡；僵硬），古英语 steorfan 原义泛指死亡，中古时期词义收窄为饿死；与 hunger、famine 等词无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: From the original meaning of dying, the word narrows to dying of hunger, then softens into everyday hunger and the act of cutting off supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从「死亡」收窄到「饿死」，再软化出日常的「饿极了」与「断供使匮乏」两个方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl no one refills, until the body burns out
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没人续添的空碗，直到身体耗尽

branches.en: dying because the food never comes
branches.cn: 因食物始终不来而死亡

branches.en: everyday exaggeration of hunger
branches.cn: 日常夸张的「饿极了」

branches.en: withholding food, money, or resources
branches.cn: 刻意不给食物、资金或资源

branches.en: the body and the appetite both run empty
branches.cn: 身体与食欲一起空掉

branches.en: the hand that cuts off the supply
branches.cn: 那只切断供应的手

intro.en: Starve is a single short root word, but its family shows how one root grew nouns and agent nouns.
intro.cn: starve 是单一短词根，其词族展示了词根如何派生出名词与施动者名词。

latinIntro.en: Starve has no Latin relatives; it is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: starve 没有拉丁同源词，属于日耳曼本土词源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

definition_zh: 会员身份；全体会员；会员人数；会费；会籍；成员关系；集合的属于关系；会员制
definition_en: the state of belonging to a group, or the members of a group taken together
core_image: 一张塑料会员卡，边缘磨得发白，卡号处有一道被反复摩挲的指印
scene: 旧图书馆的借书台前，管理员把一张磨旧的卡片推回来，说补缴费用后名字才会重新留在名册上。 At the old library desk the clerk pushed back a worn card and said her membership would be renewed once the fee was paid.
sceneCN: 这里 membership 指「会员身份」（第 1 个义项：某人作为会员的资格）；句意为管理员把磨旧的卡片推回来，说补缴费用后她的会员身份才会续上。可辨识物件：借书台、磨白的卡片、名册、印章；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 会员身份；全体会员；会员人数；会费；会籍；成员关系；（数学）属于关系；会员制

derivatives.zh: 基础词：成员；会员
非会员；未入会者（non- + member）
复合名词：由会员身份与卡片合成的会员卡，用来证明身份

senses.title: A place on the roll
senses.definition: the state of being a member of a group or organization
senses.definitionCN: 作为某团体或组织的成员而具有的身份
senses.example: Membership gives you a vote at the annual meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会员身份让你在年会上拥有投票权。
senses.why: The suffix -ship names a condition rather than a person: a member is who you are, and membership is the standing that follows.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 命名的是状态而非人：成员是你是「谁」，而会员身份是随之而来的地位。

senses.title: Everyone on the roll
senses.definition: the members of an organization considered as one group
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个整体来看的某组织的全体成员
senses.example: The whole membership was invited to the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 全体会员都应邀参加了投票。
senses.why: A collective noun is a short step from the state: if everyone holds the status, the status can name everyone.
senses.whyCN: 从状态到集体名词只差一步：如果人人都拥有这个身份，这个身份就可以用来指所有人。

senses.title: The number counted
senses.definition: the total number of members in a body
senses.definitionCN: 某组织的成员总人数
senses.example: Membership fell below two hundred last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年会员人数降到了两百以下。
senses.why: Once a roll exists it can be counted, and the abstract noun takes on a number.
senses.whyCN: 名册一旦存在就可以清点，这个抽象名词于是带上了数字。

senses.title: The fee on the counter
senses.definition: the amount paid regularly in order to remain a member
senses.definitionCN: 为保留成员身份而定期缴纳的费用
senses.example: The annual membership is due in January.
senses.exampleCN: 年度会费在一月到期缴纳。
senses.why: Institutions turned the status into something sold by the year, and the price borrowed the name of what it bought.
senses.whyCN: 机构把身份变成按年出售的东西，价格便借用了它所购买之物的名字。

senses.title: The term of the card
senses.definition: the period during which a person's status as a member lasts
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的成员身份持续的那段时间
senses.example: She let her membership lapse after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家之后，她的会籍就中断了。
senses.why: A status that can be renewed must also have an end, so the noun covers the span as well as the state.
senses.whyCN: 可以续期的身份也必然有终点，因此这个名词既指状态，也指那段时间。

senses.title: One body inside another
senses.definition: the position of a state or organization as a member of a larger body
senses.definitionCN: 国家或组织作为更大机构成员的地位
senses.example: Membership in the union requires unanimous consent.
senses.exampleCN: 加入该联盟需要全体一致同意。
senses.why: The word leaves persons behind: whole countries can hold membership in a body above them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词越过了个人：整个国家也能在更高一级的机构中拥有成员地位。

senses.title: Belonging to a set
senses.definition: in mathematics, the relation of an element to the set that contains it
senses.definitionCN: 数学中元素与其所属集合之间的关系
senses.example: The proof rests on the membership of every point in the interval.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明依赖于区间内每一点都属于该集合。
senses.why: Logic needed a precise word for one thing being inside another, and borrowed the everyday noun.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要一个精确的说法来表示一物处在另一物之中，于是借用了这个日常名词。

senses.title: Sold as a scheme
senses.titleCN: 作为制度出售的会员资格
senses.definition: used before another noun for a paid scheme that grants member benefits
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一名词前，指授予会员权益的付费制度
senses.example: The store pushed its membership programme in every aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店在每条过道里推销它的会员制度。
senses.why: Commerce compressed the whole relationship into a label, and the label itself became a product.
senses.whyCN: 商业把整段关系压缩成一个标签，而标签本身又成了商品。

intro.en: Membership joins member, from Latin membrum 'limb, part', to the Old English suffix -scipe 'state, condition'. Latin had already extended the limb word to a person who is a part of a body. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: membership 由 member 加古英语后缀 -scipe（表状态、身份）构成；member 来自拉丁 membrum「肢体、部分」。拉丁语已把这个指肢体的词扩展到「作为一个机体之部分的人」。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Membrum meant a limb or a part of the body, and Latin writers extended it to persons as parts of a community. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for cutting, but that account is a reconstruction rather than a proven form.
items.cn: membrum 意为肢体或身体的一部分，拉丁作者已把它扩展到「共同体之部分的个人」。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「切割」的词根有关，但该说法属重构，并非已证形式。

items.en: -scipe formed nouns of state and condition, as in freondscipe 'friendship'. It is generally thought to be connected with the verb for shaping or creating, and it is the direct source of the modern suffix.
items.cn: -scipe 构成表状态与身份的名词，如 freondscipe「友谊」。它一般被认为与表示「塑造、创造」的动词有关，是现代后缀的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed membre from Old French in the thirteenth century, and the -b- spelling settled later under Latin influence.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪从古法语借入 membre，拼写中的 -b- 后来在拉丁语影响下固定下来。

items.en: From the sixteenth century member and -ship combined for the state of being a member. The collective sense and the fee sense followed in later commercial use.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，member 与 -ship 组合表示成员身份。集体义与会费义在此后的商业用法中相继出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the root of membrum is a reconstruction, and the first use of the combined noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：membrum 的词根属重构，这个组合名词的首见年代也无确切记录。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words and two near look-alikes whose roots are unrelated; group two holds the words for belonging to an organization.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，另加两个字形相近却词根无关的词；第二组是表示「归属于某组织」的词。

entries.definition: The person on the roll; membership is the standing that person holds, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 名册上的那个人；membership 是此人所拥有的身份，而不是人本身。

entries.definition: To cut off the limbs of a body, built on the limb sense; it has nothing to do with lists of members.
entries.definitionCN: 切去肢体，建在「肢体」这一义上；它与成员名单毫无关系。

entries.definition: Built on memor 'mindful', not on membrum: it means the act of recalling, despite the similar sound.
entries.definitionCN: 建在 memor「留心的」之上而非 membrum：意为回忆，尽管读音相近。

entries.definition: Shares only the -ship ending; the base is champion, from Latin campus by way of a contest in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 只共用 -ship 后缀；基础词是 champion，经「场地上的竞技」这一路径上溯到拉丁 campus。

entries.definition: A formal connection with a body, often only a listed institution; membership carries rights, dues and a place on the roll.
entries.definitionCN: 与某机构的正式联系，常只是登记一个所属单位；membership 则含权利、会费与名册上的位置。

entries.definition: An organized group of people, or the act of joining; membership is the status inside such a group.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的人群团体，或加入这一团体的行为；membership 是身处其中的身份。

entries.definition: The payment that keeps a service or publication coming; membership may involve a subscription, but it also grants a status.
entries.definitionCN: 维持服务或刊物送达的付款；membership 可能包含订阅费，但它还授予一种身份。

entries.definition: The act of registering on a course or list; membership is the state that follows enrolment.
entries.definitionCN: 在课程或名单上登记的行为；membership 是登记之后持续的状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin limb word, the real suffix of state, and the real phrases used on forms and at counters.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「肢体」词、真实的状态后缀，以及表格与柜台上真实使用的搭配。

normal.en: Member is a limb of a body, and a member is a limb of an organization: the same picture at two scales.
normal.cn: 成员是团体的「肢体」，也是组织的「一肢」：同一幅图在两个尺度上重复。

normal.en: The suffix -ship works the same way in friendship, hardship and membership: it turns a base into a state.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 在 friendship、hardship 与 membership 中作用相同：把基础词变成一种状态。

normal.en: Forms say membership card and membership fee, which is where most people meet the word.
normal.cn: 表格上写会员卡与会费，多数人正是从这里认识这个词。

normal.en: A life membership lasts as long as the person; an annual one must be renewed.
normal.cn: 终身会员资格持续到人离世，年度会籍则必须续期。

normal.en: The plural memberships covers several separate memberships held at once.
normal.cn: 复数 memberships 指同时持有的几份会员资格。

abstract.en: Picture a card worn pale at the edges because a thumb has checked it at the door for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片边缘被磨得发白，因为多年来在门口被拇指反复核对。

abstract.en: Picture a roll on the wall with a tick beside each name, and one line left blank.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一份名册，每个名字旁有一个勾，只留一行空白。

abstract.en: Picture a country's flag hung inside a larger hall, one flag among many.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家的旗子挂在一座更大的会堂里，众多旗子中的一面。

examples.en: Membership in the society is open to anyone who applies.
examples.cn: 该学会的会员资格向所有申请者开放。

examples.en: The club raised its membership fee by ten percent.
examples.cn: 这家俱乐部把会费提高了百分之十。

examples.en: Total membership has doubled since the new branch opened.
examples.cn: 自新分部开设以来，会员总数翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「member（成员）+ ship（船）」——一张船票把你载进名册 → 会员身份、会籍

root: member（拉丁 membrum「肢体、部分」，引申为团体之一员）+ 古英语 -scipe（表状态、身份）；「肢体属于身体」→「人属于团体」。membrum 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one card: the standing it proves, the whole roll behind it, the number on that roll, the fee that keeps the name there, the term before renewal, a body that holds membership in a larger body, an element inside a set, and the paid scheme that sells the whole arrangement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一张卡片展开：卡片所证明的身份、卡片背后的整份名册、名册上的人数、让名字留在名册上的会费、续期之前的期限、一个机构在更大机构中的成员地位、集合中的元素关系，以及把整套安排当作商品出售的会员制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plastic card worn pale at the edges, checked at the door for years.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张边缘磨白的塑料卡片，多年来在门口被反复核对。

branches.en: STATE AND TERM: a place on the roll, and the span of time for which the card stays valid.
branches.cn: 身份与期限：名册上的一个位置，以及卡片保持有效的那段时间。

branches.en: THE ROLL AND ITS COUNT: the members taken together, and the number they add up to.
branches.cn: 名册与清点：合在一起看的全体成员，以及他们累计出的人数。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF THE CARD: the fee that keeps the name on the roll.
branches.cn: 卡片的价格：让名字留在名册上的那笔会费。

branches.en: BODY INSIDE BODY: a state or organization holding membership in a larger union.
branches.cn: 机构之中的机构：国家或组织在更大联盟中的成员地位。

branches.en: LOGIC AND COMMERCE: belonging to a set, and the paid scheme that sells the status.
branches.cn: 逻辑与商业：元素属于集合，以及把身份当作商品出售的会员制。

intro.en: Membership is member plus a suffix of state, and member itself goes back to the Latin word for a limb.
intro.cn: membership 是 member 加一个表状态的后缀，而 member 本身可上溯到拉丁语表示「肢体」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin membrum gives member; Old English -scipe gives the modern -ship, and -s marks the plural. The Latin word has no verb in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 membrum 给出 member；古英语 -scipe 给出今天的 -ship，-s 标示复数。这个拉丁词在这一词族中没有对应的动词。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是整个词族的基础。

items.structure: membrum + -er (English form of the Latin noun)
items.example: Each member of the team signed the card.
items.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。

items.example: The members voted on the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 成员们对这项提案进行了表决。

items.example: Membership gives you a vote at the annual meeting.
items.exampleCN: 会员身份让你在年会上拥有投票权。

items.example: He holds memberships in two learned societies.
items.exampleCN: 他在两个学会都拥有会员资格。

items.example: Nonmembers pay a higher entrance fee.
items.exampleCN: 非会员需付更高的入场费。

items.meaning: to cut off the limbs of a body
items.example: The old penalty was to dismember the body.
items.exampleCN: 古代的刑罚是把身体肢解。

items.meaning: the act or result of cutting apart
items.example: The chronicle records the dismemberment of the kingdom.
items.exampleCN: 编年史记下了王国的分裂。

definition_zh: 认出；承认；赏识；识别
definition_en: the act of knowing someone or something again; the acceptance of a fact; public praise; matching by machine
core_image: 门禁摄像头扫过脸庞，屏幕跳出名字
scene: 门禁摄像头扫过一张脸，屏幕上跳出熟悉的名字。 The system uses facial recognition to unlock the door.
sceneCN: 这里 recognition 是「识别」（第 4 个义项：机器认出对象）；句意为系统用人脸识别来开门。画面里可留意：扫过脸庞的摄像头、跳出的名字。

senses.title: The act of knowing again
senses.definition: the act of identifying someone or something as already known
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物辨认出为已知对象的行为
senses.example: He stared at her without recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 他盯着她，却没有认出她。
senses.why: Recognoscere meant to know again, and the noun names that second knowing.
senses.whyCN: recognoscere 意为「再一次认识」，这个名词正指这第二次认识。

senses.title: The acceptance of a fact
senses.definition: the act of admitting that something is true or official
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事为真或为官方事实的行为
senses.example: The new state won official recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新国家获得了官方承认。
senses.why: To know again is also to admit what one already knew, so the word covers formal acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 「再一次知道」也是承认自己早已知道的事，因此这个词涵盖正式承认。

senses.title: Public praise
senses.definition: the appreciation and honour that a person or a work receives from others
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一部作品从他人那里得到的欣赏与荣誉
senses.example: She received recognition for her research.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究获得了认可。
senses.why: When a group knows a person's worth again and again, that knowledge becomes honour.
senses.whyCN: 当一个群体一次次看见某个人的价值，这种认识就变成荣誉。

senses.title: Matching by machine
senses.definition: the process by which a computer identifies a face, a voice, or a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 计算机辨认面孔、声音或图案的过程
senses.example: The system uses facial recognition to unlock the door.
senses.exampleCN: 系统用人脸识别来开门。
senses.why: A machine that matches a pattern knows it again, so the old word fits the new technology.
senses.whyCN: 能匹配图案的机器，就是「再一次认出」它，于是旧词恰好适用于新技术。

intro.en: Recognition is the noun of knowing again: a face, a fact, a person's worth, and a digital pattern.
intro.cn: recognition 是「再次认识」的名词：一张脸、一个事实、一个人的价值，以及一段数字图案。

items.en: Cognoscere meant to know or learn, the root of cognition and recognition.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为认识或得知，是 cognition 与 recognition 的词根。

items.en: Recognoscere added re-, again, to cognoscere, giving the sense of knowing again.
items.cn: recognoscere 在 cognoscere 前加 re-（再次），得到「再一次认识」。

items.en: Recognitio named the act of calling something back to mind.
items.cn: recognitio 指把某物重新唤回心里的行为。

items.en: Old French reconnaissance carried the word into English as a survey or a knowing again.
items.cn: 古法语 reconnaissance 把这个词带入英语，指勘察或再次确认。

items.en: Modern English uses recognition for memory, for diplomacy, for honour, and for machine matching.
items.cn: 现代英语用 recognition 表记忆、外交、荣誉，以及机器匹配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for identification and approval.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表辨认与认可的词。

entries.definition: The mental process of knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 认知。

entries.definition: A firm belief or a court ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定信念；定罪。

entries.definition: The starting of a fire or engine.
entries.definitionCN: 点火；点火装置。

entries.definition: The act of naming what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 识别；身份确认。

entries.definition: The act of admitting or thanking.
entries.definitionCN: 承认；致谢。

entries.definition: The act of receiving something as valid.
entries.definitionCN: 接受；认可。

entries.definition: Recognition of value or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 欣赏；赏识。

normalIntro.en: The word is knowing plus again: the second knowing is recognition.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「知道」加「再一次」：第二次知道，就是 recognition。

normal.en: Cognition is knowing; recognition is knowing again.
normal.cn: cognition 是知道，recognition 是再一次知道。

normal.en: Beyond recognition means changed so much that you cannot know it again.
normal.cn: beyond recognition 意为变化太大，再也认不出来。

normal.en: In recognition of is the phrase on a prize or a certificate.
normal.cn: in recognition of 是奖状上的常用短语。

normal.en: Facial recognition is a machine doing the knowing again.
normal.cn: facial recognition 是机器在做「再一次知道」。

normal.en: Keep the g in the middle: recognition, not recongition.
normal.cn: 中间的 g 要保留：recognition，而不是 recongition。

abstract.en: Recognition is the moment when the past and the present meet in one look.
abstract.cn: 认出，是过去与当下在一个目光里相遇的瞬间。

abstract.en: To be recognized is to be told that one's existence counts.
abstract.cn: 被认出，就是被告知自己的存在算数。

abstract.en: A machine that recognizes faces is learning the oldest human act.
abstract.cn: 识别人脸的机器，正在学习最古老的人类行为。

examples.en: He stared at her without recognition.
examples.cn: 他盯着她，却没有认出她。

examples.en: The new state won official recognition.
examples.cn: 这个新国家获得了官方承认。

examples.en: She received recognition for her research.
examples.cn: 她的研究获得了认可。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 cognition（认知）：再一次认出，就是 recognition——认出、承认、赏识都由此而来。

root: 拉丁 cognoscere（认识）→ recognoscere（再认识）→ recognitio（认出）→ 古法语 reconnaissance → 英语 recognition；同族有 recognize、recognizable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is knowing again; the senses move from a face to a fact, to honour, and to a machine match.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「再一次认识」；义项从一张脸，到事实，到荣誉，再到机器匹配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camera sweeping a face, a name appearing on the screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：摄像头扫过脸庞，屏幕上跳出名字。

branches.en: a friend seen across a street
branches.cn: 在街对面看见朋友

branches.en: a treaty signed by two states
branches.cn: 两国签署的条约

branches.en: a medal placed in a hand
branches.cn: 把奖章放进一只手里

branches.en: a screen showing a name
branches.cn: 屏幕上显示的名字

branches.en: a human and a machine both knowing again
branches.cn: 人与机器都在「再一次认识」

intro.en: The word is built on the Latin verb of knowing, with a prefix of repetition and a noun ending of result.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语的「认识」动词上，加上表重复的前缀与表结果的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cognoscere, to know, changed by re- and named by -itio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cognoscere（认识），由 re- 加以改变，并由 -itio 名词化。

definition_zh: 安全；保障措施；保安；证券
definition_en: the state of being safe from harm; measures that protect people or property; a financial document that proves ownership
core_image: 门口站岗的保安与上锁的保险库，一切都被守护着
scene: 演唱会前场馆加强了人员检查，观众都感到踏实。 The airport raised its security before the holiday rush.
sceneCN: 这里 security 是「安保措施」（第 2 个义项：为防危险而采取的行动）；句意是机场在假期高峰前提升了安保级别。

derivatives.zh: security 的动词与形容词同根形式，义为「使安全；牢固的」
加 -ize 动词后缀，义为「把资产证券化」
加否定前缀 in-，义为「不安全感」

senses.title: The state of being safe
senses.definition: the condition of not being in danger or of not being attacked
senses.definitionCN: 没有危险、不被攻击的处境
senses.example: The treaty promised security for both nations.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承诺保障两国的安全。
senses.why: The locked vault means nothing inside gets hurt — the calm state after protection.
senses.whyCN: 上锁的金库意味着里面的东西毫发无损——被保护后的安稳状态。

senses.title: Measures that protect people or things
senses.definition: actions and systems designed to prevent crime, attack, or loss
senses.definitionCN: 为防犯罪、袭击或损失而设计的行动与制度
senses.example: Show your passport at the security check.
senses.exampleCN: 在安检处出示护照。
senses.why: The guards, locks and cameras are the active version of the locked door.
senses.whyCN: 保安、门锁与摄像头就是「那扇锁着的门」的动态版本。

senses.title: People who guard a place
senses.definition: people employed to watch over a building or event
senses.definitionCN: 受雇看守建筑或活动的人员
senses.example: Security stopped him at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 保安在入口处拦住了他。
senses.why: The protectors themselves take the name of what they provide.
senses.whyCN: 守护者以他们所提供的东西为名。

senses.title: Money or property pledged for a loan
senses.definition: assets promised to a lender in case the debt is not repaid
senses.definitionCN: 为贷款提供的资产，若不还债即被收走
senses.example: He offered his house as security for the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿房子为贷款作抵押。
senses.why: What is locked in the vault can be claimed if promises break.
senses.whyCN: 金库里锁着的东西，一旦承诺落空便可被取走。

senses.title: Financial instruments that prove ownership
senses.definition: documents such as stocks and bonds that show investment or debt
senses.definitionCN: 股票、债券等表明投资或债权关系的凭证
senses.example: Government securities are considered very safe investments.
senses.exampleCN: 政府证券被视为非常安全的投资。
senses.why: A pledged promise in writing becomes a tradable object — safety turned into paper.
senses.whyCN: 被抵押的书面承诺变成可交易的对象——安全感被写成了纸。

intro.en: From Latin securitas, the noun form of securus (free from care).
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 securitas，即 securus（无忧的）的名词形式。

items.en: The root behind Latin cura again means to care or pay attention.
items.cn: 与拉丁语 cura 同源的重构词根，仍表「留意、操心」。

items.en: Securitas means freedom from care and danger, formed from securus with the noun ending -tas.
items.cn: 拉丁语 securitas 由 securus 加名词后缀 -tas 构成，意为「无忧无险」。

items.en: Old French seurte carried the meaning of safety and certainty.
items.cn: 古法语 seurte 承载了安全与确定之义。

items.en: Forms like seurete reached England through law and commerce.
items.cn: seurete 等形式经法律与商业渠道传入英格兰。

items.en: English security first meant freedom from care, then protection and legal pledge.
items.cn: 英语 security 先表「无忧」，后发展出保护与法律担保义。

items.en: Modern use spans safety, guarding services, collateral, and financial securities.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖安全、安保服务、抵押品与金融证券。

note.en: Look-alikes around the -urity spelling, and nearby words in the protection field.
note.cn: -urity 拼写附近的形近词，以及保护义场的近义词。

entries.definition: the desire to learn or know
entries.definitionCN: 好奇心——与 security 拼写相近且同含 cura 词源，但语义相反方向：一个向外探，一个向内守

entries.definition: the state of being unknown or unclear
entries.definitionCN: 晦涩；无名——拼写与 security 相近，但词根不同，注意区分

entries.definition: a person or thing that guarantees a promise
entries.definitionCN: 保证人；担保——与 security 的抵押义项直接同源

entries.definition: the condition of being safe from harm
entries.definitionCN: 安全——泛指无危险，security 更强调主动的防护体系

entries.definition: the act of keeping someone or something safe
entries.definitionCN: 保护——强调动作，security 既指状态也指制度

entries.definition: a formal promise that something will happen
entries.definitionCN: 担保——与抵押义项相近，但 guarantee 偏承诺，security 偏实物

normalIntro.en: Hooks anchored in the -ity noun ending and the guard-at-the-door picture.
normalIntro.cn: 锚定在 -ity 名词后缀与门口保安画面上的记忆钩子。

normal.en: secure + -ity: the noun form of secure
normal.cn: secure 加 -ity 就是它的名词形式

normal.en: curiosity and security share the cura root but pull opposite ways
normal.cn: curiosity 与 security 同源却方向相反：一个好奇外探，一个守成

normal.en: the airport guard is the human face of this word
normal.cn: 机场保安就是这个词的人格化形象

normal.en: securities in finance are assets locked in as guarantees
normal.cn: 金融里的 securities 是被锁进来作担保的资产

normal.en: in- flips it: insecurity is the feeling of no protection
normal.cn: 加 in- 就反转：insecurity 是失去保护的感觉

abstract.en: Picture a guard with a clipboard standing at every door
abstract.cn: 想象每个门口都站着拿登记板的保安

abstract.en: See camera lights blinking quietly over a sleeping city
abstract.cn: 看见摄像头在沉睡的城市上空静静闪烁

abstract.en: Feel the weight of the key chain in the night watchman's pocket
abstract.cn: 体会守夜人口袋里钥匙串沉甸甸的分量

examples.en: Tight security kept the ceremony running smoothly.
examples.cn: 严密的安保让典礼顺利进行。

examples.en: She sold her securities to fund the new clinic.
examples.cn: 她卖掉证券为新诊所筹资。

examples.en: A steady job gave him a sense of security.
examples.cn: 稳定的工作给了他安全感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「色库里提」——从色库（仓库）里提东西？不行，得先过保安这一关，安保与证券的意思全在里面。

root: 拉丁语 securus（无忧的）+ 名词后缀 -tas 构成 securitas「无忧无险的状态」；经古法语 seurte 进入英语。抵押与证券义由「被锁住作担保的财产」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: One picture, four uses: the calm state, the guarding system, the pledged asset, the paper claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个画面，四种用法：安稳状态、守护体系、抵押资产与纸面凭证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guard at the vault door, everything watched and safe
core.cn: 核心意象：金库门口的保安，一切被看守、被守护

branches.en: the quiet that comes when danger is kept out
branches.cn: 危险被挡在外面后的安宁

branches.en: the guards, cameras and checks that make the calm
branches.cn: 保安、摄像头与安检共同造就这份安宁

branches.en: the vault contents promised to a lender
branches.cn: 金库里的东西被许诺给债主

branches.en: the promise turned into tradable paper
branches.cn: 承诺变成了可交易的纸

branches.en: protection and peace are two sides of one door
branches.cn: 保护与安宁是同一扇门的两面

intro.en: Nouns and verbs built from the secure family and the -ity ending.
intro.cn: 由 secure 词族与 -ity 后缀构成的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nouns in the cura family.
latinIntro.cn: cura 词族里的拉丁名词。

items.example: Purity means the state of being pure.
items.exampleCN: purity 表示「纯净」这一状态。

items.example: Securitas was also a Roman goddess.
items.exampleCN: Securitas 还是罗马的安全女神。

items.example: Security was tight at the summit.
He acted as surety for his brother.

items.exampleCN: 好奇心驱动每位科学家。

items.example: His insecurity showed in his silence.

items.meaningCN: 无名；晦涩——形近但词源不同，来自 obscurus（黑暗的）
items.example: The poet lived in obscurity for years.
items.exampleCN: 这位诗人默默无闻多年。

definition_zh: 额外的；附加的；另外的；追加的
definition_en: extra, or added on top of what already exists, without replacing any part of it
core_image: 账单下面又添了一行：原来那份一分没少，只是多出一行
scene: 食堂的米饭不够，师傅又端来一锅，还添了几样小菜。 There is an additional charge for the second bowl of rice.
sceneCN: 这里 additional 是「额外的收费」（第 1 个义项：在原价之外另加的钱）；句意为第二碗米饭要另外收费。

pos.zh: 形容词：额外的；附加的；另外的；追加的

forms.label: 原级（非分级形容词，无常用比较级）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「此外；另外」
本词的名词形式，由动词加名词后缀 -ition 构成，义为「添加；增加物；加法」
本词的动词原形，义为「添加；加上；相加」

senses.title: Extra money to be paid
senses.definition: of a charge, fee or cost, added to the basic price and paid on top of it
senses.definitionCN: 指收费、费用或成本在基本价格之外另加，需要额外支付
senses.example: There is an additional charge for the second bowl of rice.
senses.exampleCN: 第二碗米饭要另外收费。
senses.why: Additional is addition plus -al: it describes whatever has been given to the bill, so the old amount still stands and one line is added.
senses.whyCN: additional 是 addition 加 -al 构成的：它形容被加到账单上的那部分，原来的数目分毫未动，只是多了一行。

senses.title: Further information or details
senses.definition: of information or details, given in order to complete or clarify what has already been provided
senses.definitionCN: 指信息或细节是为了补全或澄清已经提供的内容而给出的
senses.example: Call this number if you need additional information.
senses.exampleCN: 需要更多信息请拨打这个号码。
senses.why: What is given here is knowledge rather than money, but it is still laid on top of what the listener already has.
senses.whyCN: 这里给出去的是知识而不是钱，但依然是叠在听者已知内容之上的补充。

senses.title: More time allowed
senses.definition: of time, allowed beyond the period that was first arranged or expected
senses.definitionCN: 指在最初安排或预计的时间之外又给出的时间
senses.example: The examiner gave us ten minutes of additional time.
senses.exampleCN: 考官多给了我们十分钟。
senses.why: Time is treated as a measured heap too: the first portion is kept, and one more portion is given to it.
senses.whyCN: 时间同样被当成一份可量的东西：原有的那份保留，再给一份叠上去。

senses.title: Extra people or seats
senses.definition: of people or places, brought in beyond the number already planned or provided
senses.definitionCN: 指人或位置在原有计划或配备之外再增添的
senses.example: The restaurant put out additional chairs for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 餐厅为婚礼多摆了一些椅子。
senses.why: The same word counts people and chairs: each new unit is added to the row without taking the place of an old one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也用来数人和椅子：每一个新单位都被加到那一排里，而不占用旧的位置。

senses.title: Extra terms in an agreement
senses.definition: of terms, conditions or rules, written into an agreement in addition to the main ones
senses.definitionCN: 指条款、条件或规则在主要条款之外又被写进协议之中
senses.example: Please read the additional terms before you sign.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前请先读一下附加条款。
senses.why: A contract is a list like any other; a new clause is given to the list and the old clauses keep their force.
senses.whyCN: 合同和别的清单一样：新条款被加进清单，旧条款的效力一条不减。

senses.title: Further evidence in a case
senses.definition: of evidence or proof, offered to strengthen what has already been presented in a case or inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 指证据或证明是为加强案件中已提交的材料而提出的
senses.example: The court allowed additional evidence from the defence.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭允许辩方提交补充证据。
senses.why: The first body of proof is left standing, and one more body is set beside it; nothing is withdrawn.
senses.whyCN: 原有的证据仍然成立，只是在旁边再摆上一份，什么也没有撤回。

senses.title: Extra help for someone who needs it
senses.definition: of help, teaching or care, provided beyond the ordinary level because someone needs more
senses.definitionCN: 指帮助、教学或照护超出常规水平，因为某人需要更多
senses.example: Pupils with additional support needs work in smaller groups.
senses.exampleCN: 需要额外支持的学生分成更小的组上课。
senses.why: The ordinary provision is not cut; another layer of help is given on top of it, which is the whole point of the word.
senses.whyCN: 常规的供给并没有减少，而是在其上再给一层帮助——这正是这个词的要害。

senses.title: An extra person covered by insurance
senses.definition: in insurance, of a driver, person or amount, included in a policy on top of the main cover
senses.definitionCN: 保险中指在主保单之外另行纳入的驾驶人、人员或金额
senses.example: The policy covers an additional driver at no extra cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单可以免费多保一名驾驶人。
senses.why: A policy is a list of covered names and sums; one more name or sum is added, and the original cover remains intact.
senses.whyCN: 保单就是一份受保名字与金额的清单：再加一个名字或一笔数目，原有的保障仍然完整。

intro.en: Additional is an English adjective made from the noun addition plus the suffix -al; the history below the noun is the history of add.
intro.cn: additional 是英语用名词 addition 加后缀 -al 构成的形容词；再往下追，就是 add 的历史。

items.en: Addere, 'to give to, put to, add', was ad-, 'to', plus dare, 'to give'. The root behind dare is a reconstructed Indo-European form.
items.cn: addere 意为「给到……上、放上去、增加」，由 ad-「向」加 dare「给」构成；dare 背后的词根是原始印欧语重构形式。

items.en: The action noun additio, 'an adding, an addition', supplied the stem addit- that passed through French into English.
items.cn: 动作名词 additio 意为「添加、增加」，提供了经法语进入英语的词干 addit-。

items.en: The noun addition is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, with both the general and the arithmetic senses.
items.cn: 名词 addition 自十四世纪起在英语中有记录，一般义与算术义并存。

items.en: The adjective additional was formed in English by adding -al to addition; the first records belong to the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 additional 是英语在 addition 后加 -al 构成的，最早记录见于十七世纪。

items.en: Its reach widened to institutions: additional support in schools, additional terms in contracts, an additional driver on a policy.
items.cn: 它的适用范围扩展到各种制度：学校的额外支持、合同的附加条款、保单上的附加驾驶人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun, adverb and verb of the same family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of extra and further.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的名词、副词与动词；近义组收表示「额外、进一步」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun from which the adjective is formed, meaning the act or thing added, or the operation of adding.
entries.definitionCN: 本词所由构成的名词，义为「添加、增加物、加法」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning besides or in addition; formed with the suffix -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「此外、另外」，由本词加后缀 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A substance added to food or fuel, or an adjective meaning relating to addition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加剂」，也可作形容词表示「添加的」，由同一词干加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: The verb at the root of the family, meaning to put one thing together with another.
entries.definitionCN: 整个词族的动词原形，义为「添加、加上、相加」。

entries.definition: More than the usual or expected amount; common in speech and often about money.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、多加的」，口语常用，常与钱有关。

entries.definition: Additional in the sense of more of the same, especially of information, action or distance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进一步的、更多的」，多指同类事物再加一层，尤用于信息、行动或距离。

entries.definition: Provided to complete or strengthen something, rather than simply to enlarge it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「补充的、辅助的」，强调补足或加强，而不只是把量变大，语气正式。

entries.definition: Kept in reserve and ready to be used if needed, as in a spare key or spare room.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「备用的」，指留作后备、需要时才用，如备用钥匙或空余房间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work through the noun addition, the adjective suffix and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子借助名词 addition、形容词后缀以及这个词常见的固定搭配来记忆。

normal.en: Additional is simply addition with the adjective suffix -al.
normal.cn: additional 就是 addition 加上形容词后缀 -al。

normal.en: At no additional cost is the phrase shops use to say the price will not go up.
normal.cn: at no additional cost 是商家说明价格不会上涨时用的固定说法。

normal.en: Additional time on an exam and additional seats in a hall are the same extra portion.
normal.cn: 考试多给的时间和大厅多摆的座位，是同一种「多出来的一份」。

normal.en: In contracts, additional terms are clauses added while the old ones stay in force.
normal.cn: 合同里的 additional terms 是新增条款，旧条款依然有效。

normal.en: The adverb additionally opens a sentence the way in addition does.
normal.cn: 副词 additionally 像 in addition 一样，用来在句首再补一层。

abstract.en: One more line under a bill: nothing above it is erased.
abstract.cn: 账单底下多出一行：上面那一行一个字也没被擦掉。

abstract.en: Extra is always measured against a first amount; without the first, there is no additional.
abstract.cn: 「额外」总要对照着先前的一份来量；没有先前那份，就谈不上额外。

abstract.en: Adding a layer makes the whole wider, not different in kind.
abstract.cn: 加一层只会让整体更宽，而不会让它变成另一种东西。

examples.en: There is an additional fee for changing the date.
examples.cn: 更改日期需要另付一笔费用。

examples.en: We need additional information before we decide.
examples.cn: 决定之前我们还需要一些补充信息。

examples.en: The airline offered additional time to rebook.
examples.cn: 航空公司多给了改签的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪申诺」——阿迪又在账单上加了一行，前面的账一条没删：额外的、附加的。

root: 由名词 addition 加形容词后缀 -al 构成；addition 出自拉丁语 additio「添加」，再往下是 addere「给到……上」，即 ad-「向」+ dare「给」。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses describe one more portion laid on an existing whole: money, information, time, people, contract terms, evidence, help, or insurance cover.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项说的都是叠在已有整体上的一份：钱、信息、时间、人、合同条款、证据、帮助，或保险保障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one new line is written under an existing bill, and everything above it stays.
core.cn: 核心意象：在已有账单下面添一行，上面的一切照旧。

branches.en: THE BILL: the basic price stands and one more sum is charged.
branches.cn: 账单线：基本价格不动，另收一笔。

branches.en: THE RECORD: details and evidence are supplied to complete what is already on file.
branches.cn: 记录线：补充信息与证据，为的是补全已经备案的材料。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the period already agreed is kept, and more is granted.
branches.cn: 时间线：原先约定的时长保留，再多给一段。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: chairs, staff and help are added for those who need more.
branches.cn: 人的线：为需要更多的人加椅子、加人手、加帮助。

branches.en: THE PAPER: clauses and policies gain one more item without losing any old one.
branches.cn: 文书线：合同与保单多一项，旧的保障一项不少。

intro.en: Additional is the noun addition with an adjective ending, and the whole family rests on the Latin verb addere.
intro.cn: additional 是名词 addition 加形容词词尾构成的，整个词族都立在拉丁动词 addere 之上。

latinIntro.en: Dare, addere and additio are recorded Latin forms; the deeper Indo-European root of dare is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: dare、addere 与 additio 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，dare 更早的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: The prefix points the giving at a target.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「给」这个动作指向一个目标。

items.example: Dare is the giving root of the family.
items.exampleCN: dare 是这个词族中表示「给」的词根。

items.meaning: to give to, put to, add
items.example: The prefix and dare formed addere.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与 dare 合成了 addere。

items.example: The noun supplied the English stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供了英语词干。
它把 addition 变成 additional。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from ad- and dare
latinEntries.meaning: to give to, put to, add

definition_zh: 信念；相信；信仰
definition_en: a feeling that something is true or real
core_image: 一个人在困境里仍攥紧拳头相信自己
scene: 落榜后她仍没丢掉对自己的信心。 Her belief in herself never faded.
sceneCN: 这里 belief 是「信念」（第 1 个义项：相信某事为真的心理状态）；句意是她对自己的信心从未消退。

derivatives.zh: belief 的动词形式，义为「相信」
由 believe 加 -able 构成，义为「可信的」
由 un- 加 believable 构成，义为「难以置信的」
由 believe 加 -er 构成，义为「信徒、相信的人」

senses.title: The feeling that something is true
senses.definition: a feeling that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 相信某事为真的心理状态
senses.example: Her belief in herself never faded.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的信心从未消退。
senses.why: This is the broad sense covering trust in facts and in people.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽的义项，涵盖对事实和对人的信任。

senses.title: A religious faith
senses.definition: a set of ideas held about a religion
senses.definitionCN: 关于宗教的一套信念
senses.example: People of many beliefs live in this city.
senses.exampleCN: 许多不同信仰的人住在这座城市。
senses.why: The same trust in unseen things became a word for religion.
senses.whyCN: 对不可见之物的同一种信任，转而指宗教。

intro.en: Belief comes from an Old English word for holding something dear.
intro.cn: belief 来自一个表示「珍视」的古英语词。

items.en: gelēafa meant a held conviction.
items.cn: gelēafa 意为「所持的信念」。

items.en: the word lost its first syllable.
items.cn: 这个词丢掉了开头的音节。

items.en: belief named both trust and religion.
items.cn: belief 同时指信任与宗教信仰。

items.en: the plural beliefs became common.
items.cn: 复数 beliefs 变得常见。

items.en: belief usually pairs with in.
items.cn: 如今 belief 常与 in 搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a syllable or ending; the near-meaning group gives trust words.
note.cn: 形近组差别在一个音节或词尾；近义组是表示信任的词。

entries.definition: to think something is true
entries.definitionCN: 相信

entries.definition: the easing of pain or worry
entries.definitionCN: 宽慰

entries.definition: much loved
entries.definitionCN: 心爱的

entries.definition: strong trust in something
entries.definitionCN: 信念

entries.definition: reliance on someone
entries.definitionCN: 信任

entries.definition: a firmly held belief
entries.definitionCN: 坚定的信念

normalIntro.en: Belief is what you hold true in your mind.
normalIntro.cn: belief 就是你心里认定为真的东西。

normal.en: The plural is beliefs, not believes.
normal.cn: 复数是 beliefs，不是 believes。

normal.en: Belief in yourself means self-trust.
normal.cn: belief in yourself 指自信。

normal.en: The verb is believe with a v.
normal.cn: 动词是带 v 的 believe。

normal.en: Beyond belief means too strange to accept.
normal.cn: beyond belief 指难以置信。

normal.en: A belief can be religious or personal.
normal.cn: 信念可以是宗教的，也可以是私人的。

abstract.en: See a fist held tight in hard times.
abstract.cn: 想象困境中紧握的拳头。

abstract.en: See a light kept on through the night.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏整夜不灭的灯。

abstract.en: See hands folded in quiet prayer.
abstract.cn: 想象静静合起的双手。

examples.en: Her belief in herself never faded.
examples.cn: 她对自己的信心从未消退。

examples.en: People of many beliefs live in this city.
examples.cn: 许多不同信仰的人住在这座城市。

examples.en: It is my belief that hard work pays off.
examples.cn: 我相信努力终有回报。

dict_mnemonic.text: be 加 lief（珍爱的），心里珍爱的东西就是信念。

root: 古英语 gelēafa 本义「珍视、认定」，与 lief（亲爱的）同源；中古英语简化为 belief，十六世纪起兼指信任与宗教信仰。

sensesIntro.en: Trust in a fact and trust in a religion both grow from the same root.
sensesIntro.cn: 对事实的信任与对宗教的信仰同出一源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fist held tight in hard times.
core.cn: 核心意象：困境中紧握的拳头。

branches.en: belief in yourself
branches.cn: 自信

branches.en: a strong belief
branches.cn: 坚定的信念

branches.en: beyond belief
branches.cn: 难以置信

branches.en: religious belief
branches.cn: 宗教信仰

branches.en: people of many beliefs
branches.cn: 持多种信仰的人

intro.en: Belief takes -s, and its verb family grows with -able, un- and -er.
intro.cn: belief 可加 -s，其动词家族还能加 -able、un-、-er。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古英语。

definition_zh: 灰尘；尘土；掸去灰尘；撒（粉末）；（书面）尘土、遗骸
definition_en: fine dry particles of earth or other material, household dirt, the act of removing it, or to scatter a powder over something
core_image: 阳光斜穿过窗缝，空气里浮着无数细小的颗粒
scene: 阳光从窗缝里照进来，空气里浮着细小的颗粒，落在架子上。 Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
sceneCN: 这里 dust 是「灰尘」（第 1 个义项：细干的土状颗粒）；句意是灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「布满灰尘的；土色的」
由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「抹布；掸子」
由本词与 pan 复合，义为「簸箕」

senses.title: Fine dry particles
senses.definition: fine dry particles of earth, rock or other material that can float in the air or settle on surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 细干土、岩石或其他材料构成的颗粒，能浮在空气中或落在表面
senses.example: Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。
senses.why: This is the physical core: matter reduced to particles small enough to be carried by air and to settle everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理核心：物质被碎成小到能被空气携带、又能落得到处都是的颗粒。

senses.title: A cloud of particles
senses.definition: a mass of dust lifted into the air, as by wind, traffic or an explosion
senses.definitionCN: 被风、车流或爆炸扬到空中的一团尘土
senses.example: A cloud of dust rose from the dry road.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的路面上扬起一团尘土。
senses.why: The same particles, once airborne, become a visible body; the noun then names the cloud rather than the surface layer.
senses.whyCN: 同样的颗粒一旦升空就成了一团可见的物体，名词于是指这团云，而不是表面那层。

senses.title: To remove dust
senses.definition: to wipe or brush dust from a surface, or to clean a room of it
senses.definitionCN: 把灰尘从表面擦掉或掸掉，或清扫房间里的灰
senses.example: She dusted the furniture before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到之前，她掸去了家具上的灰。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: the particles are there, and the action takes them away.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词反过来：颗粒已经在那里，动作则把它们拿走。

senses.title: To scatter a powder
senses.definition: to scatter a fine powder over something, as sugar, flour or a chemical
senses.definitionCN: 把细粉撒在某物上，如糖、面粉或化学品
senses.example: Dust the cake with a little sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 在蛋糕上撒一点糖。
senses.why: If dust can be removed, it can also be applied: the verb works in both directions, taking away or sprinkling on.
senses.whyCN: 既然灰尘能被去掉，也能被施加：这个动词两个方向都成立，拿走或者撒上。

senses.title: The ground or mortal remains
senses.definition: used in literary and religious language for the ground, the human body or what remains of it
senses.definitionCN: 用于文学与宗教语言，指土地、人体或其遗留之物
senses.example: The old prayer repeats that we are dust and return to dust.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的祷文反复说，我们本是尘土，也要归于尘土。
senses.why: Because the body returns to the ground, dust became a solemn image for mortality, fixed in the phrase dust to dust.
senses.whyCN: 因为身体归入土地，dust 成了关于必死的庄重意象，固定在 dust to dust 这一短语里。

intro.en: Dust is an Old English noun shared across the Germanic languages; the verb came later from the noun.
intro.cn: dust 是古英语名词，为多种日耳曼语言共有；动词是后来从名词变来的。

items.en: The word is sometimes connected with a root for smoke or fine vapour, but the evidence is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词有时被联系到一个表示「烟、细雾」的词根，但证据不确定。

items.en: The Germanic noun for dust is reconstructed in a form close to dustam, with relatives in several modern languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「灰尘」的名词被重构为接近 dustam 的形式，在多种现代语言中都有亲属词。

items.en: Old English dust meant dust or powder, and it was already used in religious language about the body.
items.cn: 古英语 dust 意为「灰尘、粉末」，当时已用于关于身体的宗教语言。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun and added the verb sense of sprinkling powder or removing dust.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词，并增加「撒粉」与「掸灰」两个动词义。

items.en: The verb dust is recorded as both removing dust and applying powder, two opposite actions.
items.cn: 动词 dust 在十六世纪已有记录，既指去掉灰尘，也指撒上粉末，两个方向相反。

items.en: Dust storm, gold dust and dust to dust show the word spread across weather, trade and ritual.
items.cn: dust storm、gold dust 与 dust to dust 展示了这个词横跨天气、贸易与仪式。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dust; the near-meaning group separates dirt, powder and soot by what they are made of.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dust 构成的词形；近义组按构成区分 dirt、powder 与 soot。

entries.definition: Covered with or full of dust; dust plus -y.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「布满灰尘的」，由 dust 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A cloth or brush for removing dust; dust plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抹布、掸子」，由 dust 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A flat container used with a brush to collect dust and dirt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「簸箕」，与扫帚配合收集灰尘和脏物。

entries.definition: A container for household rubbish; dust plus bin, common in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾桶」，由 dust 加 bin 构成，常见于英式英语。

entries.definition: Unclean matter such as mud or grime; it is coarser and often wetter than dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「污物、泥垢」，比 dust 更粗、更常带湿。

entries.definition: A dry substance ground into fine particles; it may be clean and deliberate, unlike dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「粉末」，指磨成细颗粒的干燥物质，可能是干净且有意制成的。

entries.definition: Black powder left by smoke; a specific kind of dust from burning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烟灰、煤烟」，是燃烧留下的一种特定灰尘。

entries.definition: Small hard particles of stone or sand; coarser and heavier than dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「砂砾」，指石或沙的小硬颗粒，比 dust 更粗更重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the particles from the air to the shelf, then show the verb working in two opposite directions.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着颗粒从空气落到架子上，再展示动词两个相反的用法。

normal.en: Dust is matter small enough to float and settle: start with a sunbeam full of specks.
normal.cn: dust 是小到能漂浮、能落下的物质：先从一道满是细点的阳光开始。

normal.en: The verb dust can mean remove dust or add powder, so the object tells you the direction.
normal.cn: 动词 dust 既可指去掉灰尘，也可指撒上粉末，看宾语就知道方向。

normal.en: Dusty, duster and dustpan all keep the same particles in view.
normal.cn: dusty、duster 与 dustpan 都围着同样的颗粒。

normal.en: A dust storm is a whole sky turned into a cloud of particles.
normal.cn: dust storm 是一整片天空都变成颗粒的云。

normal.en: Dust to dust is the solemn phrase for the body returning to the ground.
normal.cn: dust to dust 是身体回归土地的庄重短语。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow beam of light crossing a room, every speck suddenly visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一道穿过房间的窄光，每一粒微尘忽然都看得见。

abstract.en: The same specks settle on a shelf, then rise again as a cloud over a dry road.
abstract.cn: 同样的微粒落在架子上，又在干燥的路面上重新升成一团云。

abstract.en: Dust is matter at its smallest and most patient, waiting on every surface.
abstract.cn: dust 是物质最小、最有耐心的形态，等在每一个表面上。

examples.en: Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
examples.cn: 灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。

examples.en: She dusted the furniture before the guests arrived.
examples.cn: 客人到之前，她掸去了家具上的灰。

examples.en: A cloud of dust rose from the dry road.
examples.cn: 干燥的路面上扬起一团尘土。

dict_mnemonic.text: dust 是阳光里浮动的细颗粒：落在架上是灰，扬在空中是尘，擦掉是掸灰，撒上是撒粉。

root: 古英语 dust「灰尘、粉末」，为日耳曼语共有词，重构形式接近 dustam；中古英语增加「撒粉」与「掸灰」的动词义，十六世纪两种相反用法均有记录。更早的印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of dust all centre on fine particles: settled on a surface, lifted as a cloud, wiped away, sprinkled on, or returned to the ground.
sensesIntro.cn: dust 的五个义项都围绕细小颗粒：落在表面、扬成云、被擦掉、被撒上，或回归土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: specks of matter floating in a beam of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光里浮动的微小颗粒。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: particles that settle on shelves, roads and windows.
branches.cn: 表面线：落在书架、道路和窗上的颗粒。

branches.en: THE AIR: the same particles lifted into a visible cloud.
branches.cn: 空气线：同样的颗粒被扬成一团看得见的云。

branches.en: THE HAND: the verb can take dust away or put powder on.
branches.cn: 手线：动词既能拿走灰尘，也能撒上粉末。

branches.en: TWO STATES: settled dust and flying dust are the same matter in different motion.
branches.cn: 两种状态：落定的灰与飞扬的尘是同一物质的不同运动。

branches.en: THE RITUAL: dust becomes a solemn image for the body and the ground.
branches.cn: 仪式线：dust 成为身体与土地的庄重意象。

intro.en: Dust is a native Germanic noun; English adds -y, -er, -ed, -ing and compounds such as dustpan and dustbin.
intro.cn: dust 是本族语日耳曼语名词；英语加 -y、-er、-ed、-ing，并构成 dustpan、dustbin 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; Latin pulvis, dust, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基础。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「布满灰尘的；土色的」
由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「抹布；掸子」
