definition_zh: 实验的；试验性的；探索性的
definition_en: relating to experiments; based on untested ideas; using new and unusual methods
core_image: 还放在试验台上、结果未定的东西
scene: 这种疗法仍处于实验阶段，尚未推广。 The treatment is still experimental and not yet widely used.
sceneCN: 这里 experimental 是「试验性的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这种疗法仍处于实验阶段，尚未推广。

derivatives.zh: 实验
通过实验地
实验；试验

senses.title: Relating to tests
senses.definition: relating to scientific experiments
senses.definitionCN: 与科学实验有关的
senses.example: The lab bought new experimental equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室购买了新的实验设备。
senses.why: The base sense simply links to experiments.
senses.whyCN: 基础义就是与实验相关。

senses.title: Not yet proven
senses.definition: based on ideas that are not yet proven
senses.definitionCN: 基于尚未被证实的想法
senses.example: The drug is still experimental.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药仍处于试验阶段。
senses.why: Being tested means the result is still open.
senses.whyCN: 处于测试中意味着结果尚未确定。

senses.title: New and unusual
senses.definition: using new and unusual methods
senses.definitionCN: 采用新颖、不寻常的方法
senses.example: The band played experimental music.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队演奏实验音乐。
senses.why: Testing becomes a style that breaks old rules.
senses.whyCN: 试验变成一种打破旧规则的风格。

intro.en: Experimental is experiment plus the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: experimental 是 experiment 加形容词后缀 -al。

items.en: Experimentum means a trial or proof.
items.cn: experimentum 意为试验或证明。

items.en: It comes from experiri, to try.
items.cn: 它来自 experiri，意为尝试。

items.en: Experiment enters English as a learned word.
items.cn: experiment 作为学术词进入英语。

items.en: -Al turns the noun into an adjective.
items.cn: -al 把名词变成形容词。

items.en: Experimental is used in science writing.
items.cn: experimental 开始用于科学写作。

items.en: Experimental also describes bold new art.
items.cn: experimental 也用于形容大胆新潮的艺术。

note.en: Experimental means test-based; experiential means experience-based.
note.cn: experimental 指基于实验，experiential 指基于体验。

entries.definition: based on direct experience
entries.definitionCN: 体验式的

entries.definition: basic or like a natural force
entries.definitionCN: 基本的；自然力的

entries.definition: showing tender feelings
entries.definitionCN: 多愁善感的

entries.definition: done as a test
entries.definitionCN: 试验的；试用的

entries.definition: not certain or final
entries.definitionCN: 试探性的；暂定的

entries.definition: temporary until confirmed
entries.definitionCN: 临时的；暂定的

normalIntro.en: Experimental means still being tested or built on tests.
normalIntro.cn: experimental 意为仍在试验中，或建立在实验之上。

normal.en: The team collected experimental data for months.
normal.cn: 团队收集了好几个月的实验数据。

normal.en: The treatment remains experimental for now.
normal.cn: 这种疗法目前仍是试验性的。

normal.en: They staged an experimental play in the park.
normal.cn: 他们在公园上演了一部实验戏剧。

normal.en: Experimental evidence supported the claim.
normal.cn: 实验证据支持了这一说法。

normal.en: The plane flew on an experimental engine.
normal.cn: 这架飞机使用实验性发动机飞行。

abstract.en: Picture a glass beaker marked with a question mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个画着问号的玻璃烧杯。

abstract.en: Imagine a plane still painted in test colors.
abstract.cn: 想象一架仍涂着测试色的飞机。

abstract.en: Think of a stage set that keeps changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不断变换的舞台布景。

examples.en: The experimental results were hard to repeat.
examples.cn: 这些实验结果很难重复。

examples.en: The doctor warned that the method was experimental.
examples.cn: 医生提醒这种方法仍是试验性的。

examples.en: They moved into an experimental style of design.
examples.cn: 他们转向了一种实验性的设计风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「experimental」是 experiment（实验）加 -al：与实验有关的，就是「实验的、试验性的」。

root: 由 experiment（实验）加形容词后缀 -al 构成，而 experiment 源自拉丁语 experimentum（试验、证明）。

sensesIntro.en: Experimental means related to experiments, not yet proven, or boldly unusual in method.
sensesIntro.cn: experimental 意为与实验有关的、尚未证实的，或方法上大胆创新的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something still under test.
core.cn: 核心意象：仍处在测试中的事物。

branches.en: The base sense links the word to tests.
branches.cn: 基础义把词与实验联系起来。

branches.en: Testing leaves the result unproven.
branches.cn: 测试意味着结果尚未证实。

branches.en: Testing becomes a bold new style.
branches.cn: 试验变成大胆的新风格。

branches.en: Test work and uncertain results go together.
branches.cn: 实验工作与不确定的结果相伴。

branches.en: Unproven methods and new art share boldness.
branches.cn: 未证实的方法与新艺术共享大胆。

intro.en: Experimental is experiment plus the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: experimental 是 experiment 加形容词后缀 -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin experimentum supplies the base of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 experimentum 提供这个词的词基。

definition_zh: 炸弹；轰炸；惨败
definition_en: a device that explodes and causes damage
core_image: 桥下被围起来的黑色装置
scene: 拆弹手小心地靠近桥下的那枚装置。 The bomb was found under the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 bomb 是「炸弹」（第 1 个义项：会爆炸并造成破坏的装置）；句意是桥下发现了一枚炸弹。

derivatives.zh: 轰炸机；投放炸弹者
炮击；连续轰炸
炮击，连续轰炸

senses.title: An explosive device
senses.definition: a device that explodes and causes damage
senses.definitionCN: 会爆炸并造成破坏的装置
senses.example: The bomb was found under the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 桥下发现了一枚炸弹。
senses.why: This is the core sense, from a word for a booming sound.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自表示轰响的词。

senses.title: To attack with bombs
senses.definition: to attack a place by dropping bombs on it
senses.definitionCN: 向某地投掷炸弹进行攻击
senses.example: Enemy planes bombed the port at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 敌机在黎明时轰炸了港口。
senses.why: The noun became a verb as soon as bombs were used in war.
senses.whyCN: 炸弹一用于战争，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: To fail badly
senses.definition: to fail completely, as a play or a film might
senses.definitionCN: 彻底失败，如戏剧或电影票房惨淡
senses.example: The new play bombed with critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这出新戏被评论界批得很惨。
senses.why: A failure that goes down like an explosion kept the image of the bomb.
senses.whyCN: 像爆炸一样轰然倒下的失败，沿用炸弹的意象。

intro.en: Bomb goes back to a Latin word for a booming noise.
intro.cn: bomb 可上溯到拉丁语中表示轰响的词。

items.en: bombus meant a deep booming sound.
items.cn: bombus 指低沉的轰响。

items.en: bombe named an exploding shell.
items.cn: bombe 指会爆炸的炮弹。

items.en: bomb entered English as a word for a shell.
items.cn: bomb 以炮弹之义进入英语。

items.en: bombing from aircraft made the verb common.
items.cn: 飞机投弹使动词用法普及。

items.en: bomb also means to fail badly in slang.
items.cn: 在俚语中 bomb 也指惨败。

note.en: The look-alike group rhymes with bomb; the near-meaning group names other explosives.
note.cn: 形近组与 bomb 押韵；近义组是其他爆炸物。

entries.definition: a tool for tidying hair
entries.definitionCN: 梳子

entries.definition: a grave or a stone grave
entries.definitionCN: 坟墓

entries.definition: a substance that can blow things apart
entries.definitionCN: 炸药

entries.definition: a small bomb thrown by hand
entries.definitionCN: 手榴弹

entries.definition: a metal case filled with explosive
entries.definitionCN: 炮弹

normalIntro.en: Bomb is a device whose name copies the sound it makes.
normalIntro.cn: bomb 这个名字模仿了它爆炸时的响声。

normal.en: Bomb and bombard share the same base.
normal.cn: bomb 与 bombard 同出一个词基。

normal.en: A time bomb explodes at a set moment.
normal.cn: 定时炸弹在设定时刻爆炸。

normal.en: The verb bomb means to attack from the air.
normal.cn: 动词 bomb 指从空中轰炸。

normal.en: A bomber is an aircraft or a person.
normal.cn: bomber 指轰炸机或投弹者。

normal.en: A bomb scare empties a building.
normal.cn: 炸弹恐吓会让整栋楼疏散。

abstract.en: See a dark object roped off on a bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象桥上被绳子围起来的黑色物体。

abstract.en: See a flash and a cloud of dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闪光与一团尘土。

abstract.en: See an empty theatre after a bad play.
abstract.cn: 想象一出烂戏之后空荡的剧场。

examples.en: The bomb was found under the bridge.
examples.cn: 桥下发现了一枚炸弹。

examples.en: Enemy planes bombed the port at dawn.
examples.cn: 敌机在黎明时轰炸了港口。

examples.en: The new play bombed with critics.
examples.cn: 这出新戏被评论界批得很惨。

dict_mnemonic.text: bomb 读起来像「邦」的一声，四个字母就模拟了爆炸那一下闷响。

root: bomb 源自拉丁语 bombus（轰响），经法语 bombe 指爆炸的炮弹，进入英语后泛指炸弹，再引申为轰炸与惨败。

sensesIntro.en: An explosive device, an attack from the air, and a complete failure.
sensesIntro.cn: 爆炸装置、空中的攻击，以及彻底的失败。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark device roped off under a bridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：桥下被围起来的黑色装置。

branches.en: a time bomb
branches.cn: 定时炸弹

branches.en: a bomb scare
branches.cn: 炸弹恐吓

branches.en: bomb a city
branches.cn: 轰炸城市

branches.en: bombing raid
branches.cn: 轰炸袭击

branches.en: the show bombed
branches.cn: 演出惨败

intro.en: Bomb takes -er and -ard to make related nouns and verbs.
intro.cn: bomb 加 -er 与 -ard 可构成相关的名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin; the items below share the idea of an explosion.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自拉丁语，下面的词都围绕爆炸这一意象。

definition_zh: 入口；条目；参赛作品；进入
definition_en: a way in, an item in a list, or a thing entered in a competition
core_image: 一扇门通向里面的房间，门边还挂着一块记录牌
scene: 博物馆的侧门只对工作人员开放。 The side entry of the museum is open only to staff.
sceneCN: 这里 entry 是「入口」（第 1 个义项：进入的通道或门）；句意：博物馆的侧门只对工作人员开放。

pos.zh: 入口；条目；参赛作品；进入

derivatives.zh: 进入；参加
入口；进入
参赛者；新成员

senses.title: A way in
senses.definition: a door, gate, or passage through which one enters
senses.definitionCN: 供人进入的门、大门或通道
senses.example: The side entry was blocked by boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 侧面的入口被箱子堵住了。
senses.why: Entry first names the act of going in, and then the place where that act happens.
senses.whyCN: entry 最初指进入的动作，随后指发生这一动作的地方。

senses.title: An item in a list or record
senses.definition: a single item written in a list, diary, dictionary, or record
senses.definitionCN: 写在清单、日记、词典或记录中的单项
senses.example: He wrote a short entry in his diary.
senses.exampleCN: 他在日记里写了一条简短的记录。
senses.why: What is entered into a book becomes an entry, so the word names one recorded item.
senses.whyCN: 被写进书里的内容成为 entry，因此这个词指一条被记录的项目。

senses.title: A competition submission
senses.definition: a person or work entered in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 报名参加比赛的人或作品
senses.example: Her entry won the photography prize.
senses.exampleCN: 她的参赛作品赢得了摄影奖。
senses.why: To enter a contest is to put something in, and the thing put in is the entry.
senses.whyCN: 参加比赛就是把某物投进去，被投进去的东西就是 entry。

senses.title: The act of entering
senses.definition: the act of going into a place, group, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 进入某地、加入某团体或协定的行为
senses.example: The country's entry into the trade agreement took years.
senses.exampleCN: 该国加入这项贸易协定花了好几年。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply the act of going in, which still appears in formal phrases.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是进入的动作，这一含义仍出现在正式短语中。

intro.en: Entry comes from Latin intrare, to enter, through Old French entree, and it keeps both the act and the place of entering.
intro.cn: entry 来自拉丁语 intrare（进入），经古法语 entree 进入英语，同时保留「进入的动作」与「进入之处」两层含义。

items.en: Intrare means to go in or enter.
items.cn: intrare 意为走进去、进入。

items.en: Intro means within or inside.
items.cn: intro 意为在内部。

items.en: Entree names both the act and the place of entering.
items.cn: entree 同时指进入的动作和进入的地点。

items.en: Entry appears with the same double sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 entry 出现时也带有这双重含义。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of a recorded item.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「记录条目」的含义。

note.en: Entry is a going-in word and a record word, so it sits near enter words and near words for access.
note.cn: entry 既表示「进入」，也表示「记录」，因此与 enter 词族及表示通行的词相邻。

entries.definition: to go into a place
entries.definitionCN: 进入

entries.definition: a way in or the act of entering
entries.definitionCN: 入口；进入

entries.definition: a person who enters
entries.definitionCN: 进入者；参赛者

entries.definition: a door or passage for entering
entries.definitionCN: 入口；通道

entries.definition: the right or way to enter
entries.definitionCN: 进入权；通道

entries.definition: permission or payment to enter
entries.definitionCN: 准许进入；入场

normalIntro.en: Entry is the noun of enter: the way in, the act of going in, or the thing you put into a list.
normalIntro.cn: entry 是 enter 的名词：进去的路、进去的动作，或你写进清单里的那一项。

normal.en: No entry means you may not go in.
normal.cn: no entry 表示禁止进入。

normal.en: A dictionary entry is one word and its explanation.
normal.cn: dictionary entry 是一个词及其解释。

normal.en: An entry form is the paper you fill in to join.
normal.cn: entry form 是报名时填写的表格。

normal.en: The plural entries covers lists and contestants alike.
normal.cn: 复数 entries 既可指多条记录，也可指多位参赛者。

normal.en: Compare entrance: entrance stresses the doorway, entry suits records and contests too.
normal.cn: 对比 entrance：entrance 强调门口，entry 还适用于记录和比赛。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow gate with a small sign beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窄门，旁边挂着一块小牌子。

abstract.en: Imagine a line written neatly in a notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象笔记本上工整地写着一行字。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed box waiting on a contest table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个封好的盒子放在比赛桌上等待评审。

examples.en: The back entry leads to a small garden.
examples.cn: 后门通向一个小花园。

examples.en: Each entry in the list has a date.
examples.cn: 清单上的每一条记录都有一个日期。

examples.en: The judges praised the youngest entry.
examples.cn: 评委称赞了最年轻的参赛作品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + try」——想进去就得试一试；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intrare（进入）→ 古法语 entree（进入；入口）→ 中古英语 entry，核心义「进入」，引申为入口与记录条目。

sensesIntro.en: Entry begins with the act of going in, then names the place, the recorded item, and the thing submitted to a contest.
sensesIntro.cn: entry 从进入的动作开始，随后指进入之处、被记录的项目以及提交参赛的作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway, with a ledger open nearby.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门，旁边摊开一本登记簿。

branches.en: The doorway is the place of entering.
branches.cn: 入口是进入发生的地点。

branches.en: A recorded item is what has been entered in a book.
branches.cn: 记录条目是被写进书里的内容。

branches.en: A contest entry is what has been entered in a competition.
branches.cn: 参赛作品是被投进比赛的东西。

branches.en: The bare act of entering is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 纯粹的进入动作是最古老的含义。

branches.en: A doorway exists for the act of entering.
branches.cn: 入口正是为了进入的动作而存在。

intro.en: Entry grows from Latin intrare and Old French entree, with English relatives enter, entrance, and entrant.
intro.cn: entry 源自拉丁语 intrare 与古法语 entree，英语亲属词有 enter、entrance 与 entrant。

latinIntro.en: Latin intrare means to enter, built on intra, within.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intrare 意为进入，建立在 intra（在内）之上。

items.example: Intra marks the inside of a place.
items.exampleCN: intra 标示一个地方的内部。

items.example: Intrare is the direct Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: intrare 是直接的拉丁语动词。

items.example: Entree carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entree 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: a way in or a recorded item
items.exampleCN: entry 保留两种古老含义。

items.example: Enter is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: enter 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: An entrant is someone who enters.
The ending of entry marks a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: entry 的词尾标示动作名词。

definition_zh: 调查；研究；侦察
definition_en: to examine a situation, event, or person carefully in order to find out the truth
core_image: 一只手举着灯，在地上一点点照着找脚印
scene: 雨后的院子里，两个人蹲下来，用手电照着泥地，看脚印往哪个方向走。 Police are investigating the cause of the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 investigate 是「调查」（第 1 个义项：为查明真相而仔细查），句意为警方正在调查火灾的起因。画面里的物件：手电、泥地脚印、警戒线。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「调查」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「调查员」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「调查性的」
同源词，义为「痕迹」

senses.title: Look into a case
senses.definition: to try to find out the facts about a crime, accident, or complaint
senses.definitionCN: 设法查清犯罪、事故或投诉的事实
senses.example: Officers are investigating the break-in at the school.
senses.exampleCN: 警员正在调查学校那次闯入事件。
senses.why: Latin vestigium means a footprint, and the verb meant to follow footprints.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vestigium 意为「脚印」，那个动词意为「循脚印追查」。

senses.title: Study to understand
senses.definition: to examine something systematically in order to understand how it works
senses.definitionCN: 为理解其运作方式而系统地检视某事物
senses.example: Scientists are investigating why the lake is warming.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家正在研究这座湖为何变暖。
senses.why: The same footprint-following works for nature as for crime.
senses.whyCN: 循脚印追查既用于案件，也用于自然现象。

senses.title: Examine a person
senses.definition: to question or examine a person officially to judge their part in something
senses.definitionCN: 为判断某人在事件中的角色而正式讯问或审查
senses.example: Two managers were investigated over the payments.
senses.exampleCN: 两名经理因这些款项受到调查。
senses.why: People also leave tracks, so the verb turns from things to persons.
senses.whyCN: 人也会留下痕迹，于是这个动词从物转向人。

senses.title: Explore a possibility
senses.definition: to look into whether something is possible or true before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在决定之前先弄清某事是否可能或属实
senses.example: We should investigate whether the hall can hold two hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 我们该查一查礼堂能不能容纳两百人。
senses.why: The cautious sense checks facts before a decision is made.
senses.whyCN: 这种谨慎用法是在决定之前先核实。

intro.en: Investigate comes from Latin investigare, to follow footprints, from vestigium, a footprint.
intro.cn: investigate 来自拉丁语 investigare「循脚印追查」，源出 vestigium「脚印」。

items.en: Vestigium meant a footprint or a trace left behind.
items.cn: vestigium 意为脚印或留下的痕迹。

items.en: Investigare meant to track something by its traces.
items.cn: investigare 意为顺着痕迹追踪。

items.en: The noun investigatio named the tracing itself.
items.cn: 名词 investigatio 指这番追踪。

items.en: English used investigate for legal and scholarly inquiry.
items.cn: 英语用 investigate 指法律与学术的查究。

items.en: Police work made it a familiar verb of daily news.
items.cn: 警务让它成为新闻里的常用动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invest- opening; the near-meaning group holds words for inquiry.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invest- 开头；近义组收表示查究的词。

entries.definition: The inquiry itself as a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「调查」。

entries.definition: To put money into something for a return.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「投资」，拼写近似。

entries.definition: A small remaining trace of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「残留的痕迹」，同出 vestigium。

entries.definition: To look at something closely and carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「检查」，偏细看。

entries.definition: To search into something awkward or hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「探究」，语气更锐利。

entries.definition: To try to find out about something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语义为「查一查」，偏口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the footprint at the heart of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用这个词心里的那只脚印。

normal.en: Vestigium means footprint; to investigate is to follow the prints.
normal.cn: vestigium 意为脚印；investigate 就是顺着脚印走。

normal.en: The same trace survives in vestige, a leftover mark.
normal.cn: 同样的痕迹留在 vestige 里，那是残余的印记。

normal.en: Police investigate crimes; scientists investigate causes.
normal.cn: 警察调查案件，科学家研究成因。

normal.en: Under investigation means the prints are still warm.
normal.cn: under investigation 意思是脚印还没凉。

normal.en: Do not mix it with invest, which is about money.
normal.cn: 别和 invest 混：那个词讲的是钱。

abstract.en: Investigation is patience with a lamp.
abstract.cn: 调查是举着灯的一点耐心。

abstract.en: Every fact leaves a print somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每个事实都会在某处留下印子。

abstract.en: To investigate is to admit you do not yet know.
abstract.cn: 调查等于承认自己还不知道。

examples.en: The committee will investigate how the money was spent.
examples.cn: 委员会将调查这笔钱是如何花掉的。

examples.en: She investigated the strange noise in the attic.
examples.cn: 她去查了阁楼里那奇怪的声音。

examples.en: He was investigated twice and cleared both times.
examples.cn: 他两次受到调查，两次都洗清了。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vestige（痕迹）+ ate——顺着痕迹查进去

root: 拉丁语 vestigium「脚印」→ investigare「循迹追查」→ 英语 investigate。同族有 investigation、investigator、vestige。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: look into a case, study how something works, examine a person, and test a possibility.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：查案、研究运作原理、审查某人，以及核实某种可能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp on the ground, following prints through mud.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏照在地上的灯，顺着泥里的脚印走。

branches.en: THE CASE: officers tracing what happened.
branches.cn: 案件这条线：警员追查发生了什么。

branches.en: THE LAKE: researchers tracing why it warms.
branches.cn: 湖这条线：研究者追查变暖的原因。

branches.en: THE MANAGER: a person questioned about payments.
branches.cn: 经理这条线：就款项受到询问的人。

branches.en: THE HALL: checking a fact before deciding.
branches.cn: 礼堂这条线：决定之前先核实。

branches.en: THE LINK: both follow traces towards a hidden cause.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都顺着痕迹追向隐藏的原因。

intro.en: Investigate is in- "in" plus the Latin stem vestig- "trace" and a verb ending.
intro.cn: investigate 是 in-「在内」加拉丁词干 vestig-「痕迹」与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestigium, investigare and investigatio are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium、investigare 与 investigatio 均有记载。

The stem also appears in vestige.

definition_zh: 放弃；抛弃；遗弃；丢弃；离弃；放任、纵情
definition_en: to leave a person, place or thing behind for good, or to stop doing something before it is finished
core_image: 摊开的手掌：原本握着的东西被松开，留在身后
scene: 洪水退去，救援队发现那辆旧卡车陷在泥里，怎么也拖不动。 They had to abandon the truck in the mud and walk to the village.
sceneCN: 这里 abandon 是「丢下、弃置」（第 1 个义项：把带不走的东西留在原地）；句意为他们只好把那辆卡车丢在泥里，步行去村里。

pos.zh: 及物动词：放弃；抛弃；遗弃；丢弃；放任、纵情
名词（多用于短语 with abandon）：放纵；尽情

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「放弃；遗弃；弃置」
由本词加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「被遗弃的；荒废的；放纵的」
由本词与 ware 复合而成，指作者已停止维护、无人负责的软件

senses.title: To leave a place or thing behind
senses.definition: to leave a place, vehicle or object behind because you can no longer keep it or take it with you
senses.definitionCN: 因无法继续保有或带走，而把地方、车辆或物件留在原地
senses.example: They had to abandon the truck in the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 他们只好把那辆卡车丢在泥里。
senses.why: Old French a bandon meant 'into someone's power': to abandon is first to hand a thing over and let go of it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 a bandon 意为「交到别人的支配之下」：abandon 最初就是把东西交出去、松开手，于是有了「丢下不管」。

senses.title: To desert a person in your care
senses.definition: to leave a person or animal that depends on you, especially when you have a duty to stay
senses.definitionCN: 离开依赖自己的人或动物，尤指在本该留下尽责的时候
senses.example: The family abandoned the puppy when they moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人搬走时把小狗遗弃了。
senses.why: The same letting-go turns cruel when the thing released is a living creature that cannot follow you.
senses.whyCN: 当被放开的是一个跟不上你的活物时，同一种「松手」就变成了残忍的遗弃。

senses.title: To stop doing something unfinished
senses.definition: to give up an activity, plan or piece of work before it is complete
senses.definitionCN: 在一项活动、计划或工作完成之前就停止不做
senses.example: The company abandoned the new railway line after two years.
senses.exampleCN: 两年后，公司放弃了那条新铁路线。
senses.why: A project is held in the hand like an object; abandoning it means opening the hand before the work is done.
senses.whyCN: 项目就像握在手里的物件；abandon 就是活还没干完就先松了手，所以有「中途放弃」。

senses.title: To give up a claim or belief
senses.definition: to relinquish a right, claim, demand or belief and stop asserting it
senses.definitionCN: 交出手中的权利、要求、主张或信念，不再坚持
senses.example: She abandoned her claim to the family land.
senses.exampleCN: 她放弃了对家族土地的主张。
senses.why: A claim is something you hold against others; letting go of it is the same release, now in law and argument.
senses.whyCN: 主张是你用来对抗别人的凭据；松开它仍是同一个「放手」动作，只是发生在法律与争论里。

senses.title: To withdraw from a match or race
senses.definition: to withdraw from a game, race or contest before it finishes, often because of weather or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因天气、伤病等原因，在比赛结束前退出竞赛
senses.example: The referee abandoned the match after the storm began.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨开始后，裁判中止了比赛。
senses.why: When the contest can no longer be carried on, the officials let the whole thing go, which is abandoning it.
senses.whyCN: 比赛已经无法继续进行时，裁判把整场比赛放开不管，这就是 abandon 用于「中止、退出」的来路。

senses.title: To give yourself over to a feeling
senses.definition: in abandon oneself to, to stop resisting an emotion or pleasure and let it take over
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 abandon oneself to，指不再抗拒某种情绪或享乐，任其支配自己
senses.example: For one evening they abandoned themselves to the music.
senses.exampleCN: 那一晚他们纵情于音乐之中。
senses.why: Here the thing released is the self: you hand your own control over to the feeling, so the old 'give over' sense turns inward.
senses.whyCN: 这里被放开的是「自己」：你把自控权交给某种感受，于是「交出」的旧义转向了内部，成了沉溺。

senses.title: With abandon: without restraint
senses.definition: in the phrase with abandon, in a free and uninhibited way, with no attempt to hold back
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 with abandon，指自由自在、毫不克制地做某事
senses.example: The children ran through the sprinklers with abandon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们毫无顾忌地在喷水器间奔跑。
senses.why: The noun keeps the state produced by letting go: once restraint is released, what is left is abandon itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「松手」之后的状态：约束一放开，剩下的就是 abandon 本身，即尽情与无所顾忌。

senses.title: Abandon ship: to leave a sinking vessel
senses.definition: in the order abandon ship, to leave a vessel that is sinking or in danger, and by extension to quit a failing enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 用于口令 abandon ship，指离开正在下沉或遇险的船，引申为退出失败的事业
senses.example: The captain gave the order to abandon ship at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船长在黎明时下令弃船。
senses.why: The most concrete case of leaving something behind is stepping off a ship that can no longer carry you.
senses.whyCN: 「丢下东西」最具体的情形，就是从一艘已经载不动你的船上走下来，这就是弃船。

intro.en: Abandon reached English from Old French, and behind the French word lies a Germanic word for a proclamation or command.
intro.cn: abandon 经古法语进入英语，古法语这个词的背后是一个表示「公告、命令」的日耳曼词。

items.en: The reconstructed Frankish form *bann meant 'a proclamation, a command'; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 重构的法兰克语形式 *bann 意为「公告、命令」，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin bannum recorded the same word as 'proclamation, ban, jurisdiction', and it also produced the verb bannire.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 bannum 记录的是同一个词，义为「公告、禁令、管辖」，并生出动词 bannire。

items.en: Old French bandon meant 'power, control'; the phrase a bandon meant 'at someone's disposal, in someone's power'.
items.cn: 古法语 bandon 意为「权力、支配」；短语 a bandon 意为「听凭某人处置、在某人掌握之中」。

items.en: From mettre a bandon, 'to put at someone's disposal', came abandonner, 'to give over, surrender, desert'.
items.cn: 由 mettre a bandon「置于他人支配之下」产生了 abandonner，意为「交出、让与、抛弃」。

items.en: English took the verb in the late fourteenth century; the noun sense of free, unrestrained behaviour is much later.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪后期借入这个动词；名词「放纵、尽情」的用法要晚得多。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the derived forms and the old Germanic relatives; the near-meaning group holds verbs of leaving, quitting and giving up.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生形式与古老的日耳曼同源词；近义组收表示离开、停止与放弃的动词。

entries.definition: the act of leaving something or someone behind, or the state of being left.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「放弃、遗弃、弃置」，指丢下某人某物的行为或状态。

entries.definition: left empty or uncared for, or given over to vice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被遗弃的、荒废的」，也可指「自甘堕落的」。

entries.definition: An official prohibition, from the same Germanic word for a proclamation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「禁令、禁止」，与 bandon 同出「公告」这一日耳曼词。

entries.definition: The public announcement of an intended marriage, read in church.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结婚公告」，教堂里公开宣读，与 abandon 同源。

entries.definition: Software that its owner no longer sells or maintains but that is still passed around.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指作者已停止销售与维护、却仍在流传的软件。

entries.definition: To leave a person or place, especially in a way that breaks a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「遗弃、弃守」，强调背弃责任，语气比 abandon 更重。

entries.definition: To give up or leave someone or something entirely; old and literary in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、舍弃」，语气古雅，多用于书面与文学。

entries.definition: To give up a right, position or control, usually willingly and formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放弃（权利、职位、控制）」，多指自愿而正式地交出。

entries.definition: To stop doing something or leave a job; plainer and less dramatic than abandon.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「停止、辞去」，口语色彩强，不似 abandon 那样带决绝意味。

entries.definition: To stop trying or stop doing something; the everyday equivalent of abandon.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「放弃、不再尝试」，是 abandon 最日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old French phrase, the Germanic relatives and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古法语短语、日耳曼同源词，以及这个词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Bandon meant control: a bandon was 'at someone's disposal', and abandonner was to hand it over.
normal.cn: bandon 意为「支配」：a bandon 就是「听凭处置」，abandonner 就是把它交出去。

normal.en: The same Germanic word gives ban and banns, both about public announcement.
normal.cn: 同一个日耳曼词还给出 ban 与 banns，两者都与公开宣告有关。

normal.en: Abandon ship is the order to step off a vessel that can no longer carry you.
normal.cn: abandon ship 是让人离开一艘已经载不动自己的船的口令。

normal.en: Abandon oneself to music is to hand control over to the music.
normal.cn: abandon oneself to music 就是把控制权交给音乐。

normal.en: With abandon keeps the noun: restraint is gone, and what remains is the letting go.
normal.cn: with abandon 保留了名词用法：约束消失，剩下的正是那份「放开」。

abstract.en: Picture open hands: nothing is taken away, everything is simply no longer held.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的手掌：东西没有被拿走，只是不再被握住。

abstract.en: The road continues after you stop walking; abandoning is your stopping, not the road ending.
abstract.cn: 你停下脚步之后路还在延伸；放弃是你停步，不是路到了尽头。

abstract.en: The same release can be cruelty, surrender or freedom, depending on what is left behind.
abstract.cn: 同一次松手可以是残忍、是屈服，也可以是自由，取决于被留下的是什么。

examples.en: They had to abandon the truck in the mud.
examples.cn: 他们只好把那辆卡车丢在泥里。

examples.en: She abandoned her plan to study abroad.
examples.cn: 她放弃了出国留学的计划。

examples.en: The children ran through the sprinklers with abandon.
examples.cn: 孩子们毫无顾忌地在喷水器间奔跑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿班等」——班车左等右等不来，索性把行李一丢走人：放弃、抛弃。

root: 古法语 a bandon（听凭处置）衍生出 abandonner（交出、抛弃），再进入英语；bandon 源自法兰克语 *bann「公告、命令」，与英语 ban、banns 同源。把 abandon 拆成 a + ban + don（给予）是后人附会，并非真实词源。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of abandon is one action of letting go; what changes is the object released: a thing, a person, a task, a claim, a match, the self, or a ship.
sensesIntro.cn: abandon 的每个义项都是同一次「松手」，变的只是被放开的对象：物件、人、任务、权利、比赛、自己，或一艘船。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of open hands, and what was held is left behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的双手，原本握着的东西被留在身后。

branches.en: THINGS AND SHIPS: what cannot be carried is left where it stands.
branches.cn: 物件与船线：带不走的东西就留在原地。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the same release becomes cruel when the one left behind depends on you.
branches.cn: 人物线：当被留下的人依赖你时，同一次松手就成了残忍。

branches.en: TASKS: the hand opens before the work or the contest is finished.
branches.cn: 任务线：活或比赛还没结束，手就先松开了。

branches.en: CLAIMS: a right or belief is handed over and no longer asserted.
branches.cn: 权利线：权利或信念被交出去，不再主张。

branches.en: THE SELF: control is given to a feeling, and the leftover state is called abandon.
branches.cn: 自我线：把控制权交给某种感受，剩下的状态就叫 abandon。

intro.en: Abandon is an Old French verb built from a preposition and a noun, and English adds its ordinary suffixes to make the family.
intro.cn: abandon 是由介词与名词构成的古法语动词，英语再加上普通后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: The base noun is Germanic in origin but was recorded in Medieval Latin as bannum, so the Latin entries below are medieval and not classical.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根名词源自日耳曼语，但以 bannum 的形式见于中世纪拉丁语，所以下面列的是中世纪拉丁语而非古典拉丁语。

items.example: a bandon meant at someone's disposal.
items.exampleCN: a bandon 意为听凭某人处置。

items.example: Bandon gave the verb its idea of handing over.
items.exampleCN: bandon 赋予这个动词「交出」的含义。

items.example: A ban is a public order not to do something.
items.exampleCN: ban 就是公开禁止做某事的命令。

items.example: The banns were read on three Sundays.
items.exampleCN: 结婚公告在三个星期日宣读。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「放弃；遗弃；弃置」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「被遗弃的；荒废的；放纵的」
由本词与 ware 复合而成，指无人维护却仍在流传的软件

definition_zh: 发动机；马达；汽车；机动的；运动（神经）的
definition_en: a machine that turns energy into movement; a car, in British informal use; and, as an adjective, relating to engine-driven vehicles or to the body's own movement
core_image: 一圈铜线圈在铁壳里旋转，把电变成持续不断的转力
scene: 修车间的木架上放着一台拆开的旧机器，铜线圈露在外面，地上掉着几颗螺丝。 A rusty electric motor lay on the bench, its copper coil exposed.
sceneCN: 这里是「电动机、马达」（第 1 个义项：把能量转成转动的机器）；句意为木架上放着一台生锈的电动机，铜线圈露在外面。图中可辨识物件：木架、铜线圈、散落的螺丝。

derivatives.zh: 由 motor 加 -ist 构成，义为「驾车者；开车的人」
由 motor 与 way 复合而成，义为「高速公路」
由 motor 加 -ize 构成，义为「使机动化；给……装上发动机」
由希腊语 autos（自己）与 motive 构成，义为「汽车的；机动车辆的」

senses.title: A machine that turns energy into movement
senses.definition: a machine that uses electricity or fuel to produce movement and drive another machine
senses.definitionCN: 用电或燃料产生运动、驱动另一台机器的装置
senses.example: The fan stopped when its motor burned out.
senses.exampleCN: 风扇的电动机烧坏后就不转了。
senses.why: Latin motor meant a mover, one that sets something else going, and English applied the name to the machine that does exactly that inside another machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 motor 意为「推动者」，即让别的东西动起来的那一方；英语把这个名字给了在另一台机器内部干这件事的装置。

senses.title: A car in British speech
senses.definition: a car, especially in informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 汽车，尤用于英式口语
senses.example: They packed the children into the motor and drove north.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把孩子们塞进车里，开车往北去。
senses.why: Once the engine was the interesting part of a vehicle, British speech began calling the whole vehicle a motor, keeping the machine's name for the thing it drove.
senses.whyCN: 当发动机成了一辆车里最要紧的部分，英式口语干脆把整辆车都叫 motor，用机器名代替它所驱动的东西。

senses.title: Belonging to engine-driven vehicles
senses.definition: connected with vehicles that have engines, or with the trade that makes and sells them
senses.definitionCN: 与装有发动机的车辆有关的，或与制造、销售这类车辆的行业有关的
senses.example: The motor trade hired fewer school leavers that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年汽车行业招收的毕业生减少了。
senses.why: The noun grew an adjective without changing shape: anything belonging to engine-driven vehicles could take the word as a label, so motor trade and motor vehicle need no suffix.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词没变形就长出了形容词用法：凡属于发动机驱动车辆的事物，直接拿这个词当标签就行，于是 motor trade、motor vehicle 都不必再加词尾。

senses.title: Belonging to the body's movement system
senses.definition: connected with the nerves and muscles that produce movement in the body
senses.definitionCN: 与身体中产生运动的神经和肌肉有关的
senses.example: The injury damaged the motor nerves in his left hand.
senses.exampleCN: 这次受伤损伤了他左手的运动神经。
senses.why: Physiologists needed a word for the body's own movers, the nerves and muscles that carry out a command, and motor was the obvious borrow from mechanics.
senses.whyCN: 生理学家需要给身体里执行指令的推动者——神经与肌肉——一个名字，于是从机械学里直接借来了 motor 这个词。

intro.en: Motor is the Latin agent noun for a mover, taken into English in the nineteenth century and then extended from engines to cars and to the body's nerves.
intro.cn: motor 是拉丁语里表示「推动者」的施动名词，十九世纪进入英语，随后从发动机扩展到汽车与身体的神经。

items.en: Movere meant to move or to set in motion, and it stands behind a large family of English words about movement.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动起来，英语里一大族与运动有关的词都出自它。

items.en: Motor was a Latin noun for the mover, the one who or that which sets something in motion, though it was much rarer than the verb beside it.
items.cn: motor 是拉丁语名词，指推动者，即让某物动起来的人或物；不过比起旁边的动词，它出现得要少得多。

items.en: English took motor with the rise of machines driven by steam and electricity, using it first for the source of motion and then for the engine itself.
items.cn: 随着蒸汽与电力驱动的机器兴起，英语借入了 motor，先指运动的来源，再指发动机本身。

items.en: By the early twentieth century British speakers were calling a car a motor, a shortening of motor car, and the word entered everyday speech.
items.cn: 到二十世纪初，英式说法开始把汽车叫作 motor，这是 motor car 的缩短形式，这个词由此进入日常口语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the engine noun, the British car noun, the vehicle adjective, and the physiological adjective for nerves and skills.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了这个名词指发动机、英式口语里指汽车、形容词指车辆，以及生理学上形容神经与技能。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin mover family; the near-meaning group collects words for engines and for the vehicles they drive.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「移动」词族展开；近义组收表示发动机以及它所驱动车辆的词。

entries.definition: Movement, or a formal proposal put to a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 运动；会议上正式提出的动议。

entries.definition: A reason that makes someone act.
entries.definitionCN: 促使人行动的理由。

entries.definition: To raise someone in rank or help something advance.
entries.definitionCN: 提升某人的职位，或推动某事进展。

entries.definition: A strong feeling that moves a person.
entries.definitionCN: 推动人的强烈情绪。

entries.definition: A machine that turns fuel into motion.
entries.definitionCN: 把燃料转成运动的机器。

entries.definition: A machine that produces electricity.
entries.definitionCN: 产生电力的机器。

entries.definition: A road vehicle with four wheels and its own engine.
entries.definitionCN: 自带发动机的四轮道路车辆。

entries.definition: A machine used for carrying people or goods.
entries.definitionCN: 用来运送人或货物的机器。

normalIntro.en: A Latin agent noun runs through the family, so every sense of the word names something that moves other things rather than something that is moved.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语施动名词贯穿这个词族，所以这个词的每个义项都在给「推动别的东西」的那一方命名，而不是被推动的一方。

normal.en: Movere is the Latin verb to move, and motor is its agent noun, the one that moves, which is why a motor is never the thing moved but the thing that moves others.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，motor 是它的施动名词，指「推动者」；所以 motor 从来不是被推动的东西，而是推动别的东西的那一方。

normal.en: The -or ending in motor is the same agent ending found in actor and doctor, so the word literally names a doer.
normal.cn: motor 里的 -or 与 actor、doctor 里的施动词尾相同，所以这个词字面上就是在给一个「做事的角色」命名。

normal.en: Motorist adds -ist to motor, a person who uses a motor vehicle, which shows how a machine name turned into a name for its driver.
normal.cn: motorist 在 motor 后加 -ist，指使用机动车的人，可见机器名如何变成了驾驶者的名字。

normal.en: Motorway is motor plus way, a road built for motor traffic, a compound that says exactly what the road is for.
normal.cn: motorway 是 motor 加 way，指为机动车修的路；这个复合词把路的用途说得明明白白。

normal.en: The physiological sense keeps the original meaning best: motor nerves are the body's own movers, the ones that carry out a command.
normal.cn: 生理学义最贴近原意：运动神经就是身体自己的推动者，负责把指令执行下去。

abstract.en: Picture a coil spinning inside an iron shell, turning current into a steady push.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈线圈在铁壳里旋转，把电流变成一股持续的推力。

abstract.en: A word that names the mover rather than the movement shows how English labels a machine by its role, not by its shape.
abstract.cn: 一个为「推动者」而不是「运动」命名的词，说明英语常按角色给机器命名，而不是按外形。

abstract.en: The same noun reaches from a factory engine to the nerves in a hand, because both are places where a command becomes motion.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词从工厂里的发动机一直伸到手上的神经，因为这两处都是「指令变成运动」的地方。

examples.en: The fan stopped when its motor burned out.
examples.cn: 风扇的电动机烧坏后就不转了。

examples.en: They packed the children into the motor and drove north.
examples.cn: 他们把孩子们塞进车里，开车往北去。

examples.en: The injury damaged the motor nerves in his left hand.
examples.cn: 这次受伤损伤了他左手的运动神经。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩托」——摩托车里的摩托就是 motor 的音译，本指推动的那台机器；记住 motor 是发动机，也指汽车。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）的施动名词 motor（推动者）进入英语，十九世纪起指发动机，二十世纪英式口语又指汽车；同族词有 motion、motive、promote、emotion。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the thing that sets something else moving; the senses divide into the engine, the British car, the vehicle adjective, and the body's own movers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「让别的东西动起来的那一方」；义项分出机器、英式口语的汽车、车辆的形容词用法，以及身体自己的推动者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a copper coil spinning inside an iron shell and turning current into a steady push.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈铜线在铁壳里旋转，把电流变成持续的推力。

branches.en: a coil spinning inside a rusted casing
branches.cn: 生锈外壳里旋转的一圈线圈

branches.en: a fan blade turning in a hot room
branches.cn: 热房间里转动的风扇叶

branches.en: children bundled into a small car on a cold morning
branches.cn: 冷天早晨被塞进一辆小车的孩子

branches.en: a factory gate where new cars roll out
branches.cn: 新车驶出的工厂大门

branches.en: a hand opening slowly after a nerve signal arrives
branches.cn: 接到神经信号后慢慢张开的手

intro.en: A Latin agent noun, the verb behind it, and a few English suffixes carry motor from a mover to engines, cars and nerves.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语施动名词、它背后的动词，以及几个英语词尾，把 motor 从「推动者」带到发动机、汽车与神经。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere and its agent noun motor supply the whole family, while motus and motivus show the movement and the force that causes it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 movere 及其施动名词 motor 支撑起整个词族，motus 与 motivus 则分别表示运动与引起运动的力量。

items.meaning: a car driven by an engine
a driver of a motor vehicle

definition_zh: 特权；特殊待遇；荣幸；拒证权；授予特权
definition_en: a special right or advantage held by a person or group; the honour of being allowed to do something; a legal right to keep certain information secret; and, as a verb, to grant such a right
core_image: 门口只发给少数人的一张通行证
scene: 老图书馆的顶层有一间不对外开放的书库，管理员把一枚铜钥匙放在桌上，说只有几位研究者可以进去。 Only a handful of readers hold the privilege of working in that locked room.
sceneCN: 这里的 privilege 是「特权、特殊待遇」（第 1 个义项：只给少数人的特别权利）；句意为只有少数读者拥有在那间上锁的书库工作的特权。图中可辨识物件：铜钥匙、上锁的书库门、登记簿。

pos.zh: 特权；特殊待遇；荣幸；拒证权

derivatives.zh: 由 privilege 加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「享有特权的；有幸的」
由 under-（不足）加 privileged 构成，义为「贫困的、被剥夺基本机会的」

senses.title: A special right held by a person or group
senses.definition: a special right or advantage that only a particular person or group enjoys
senses.definitionCN: 只有特定的人或群体才享有的特别权利或好处
senses.example: Members of the club enjoy privileges that outsiders cannot buy.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部成员享有外人花钱也买不到的特权。
senses.why: Latin privilegium was a law aimed at one individual, so the word began as a rule made for a single person rather than for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 privilegium 是专门针对某一个人立的法，所以这个词从一开始就是「为一个人单独定的规矩」，而不是对所有人通用的规矩。

senses.title: The honour of being allowed to do something
senses.definition: a special honour that comes from being given the chance to do something
senses.definitionCN: 因为获得做某事的机会而感到的一种特别的光荣
senses.example: It was a privilege to hear the old pianist play one last time.
senses.exampleCN: 能听这位老钢琴家最后一次演奏，是一种荣幸。
senses.why: If a right is granted to few people, receiving it feels like being chosen, and that feeling of being singled out is the honour sense.
senses.whyCN: 既然一项权利只授予少数人，得到它就像被选中，这种「被单独挑出来」的感受就是「荣幸」这一义。

senses.title: A legal right to keep certain information secret
senses.definition: a legal protection that lets a person or a professional refuse to reveal certain information
senses.definitionCN: 允许某个人或某种职业者拒绝透露某些信息的法律保护
senses.example: Lawyers may claim privilege over what a client tells them.
senses.exampleCN: 律师可以就当事人告知的内容主张保密特权。
senses.why: Courts borrowed the word for rights that shield a conversation from being used as evidence, keeping the old idea of a protected space.
senses.whyCN: 法庭借这个词来指「让某段谈话不被用作证据」的权利，保住的还是那个老意象：围起来的一小块受保护的空间。

senses.title: To grant someone a special right or honour
senses.definition: to give a person or group a special right, advantage, or honour that others do not have
senses.definitionCN: 给予某个人或群体一种别人没有的特别权利、好处或光荣
senses.example: The charter privileges the port city with its own customs rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这份特许状授予这座港口城市自定海关规则的权力。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by putting the thing granted in the object slot: to privilege someone is to hand them the very advantage the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，只要把被授予的东西放进宾语位置：to privilege someone 就是把这个名词所指的那份好处交到某人手里。

intro.en: Privilege is a Roman legal term: two Latin words, one for a single person and one for law, were joined into a name for a law aimed at one case.
intro.cn: privilege 是一个罗马法术语：两个拉丁词，一个表示单个的人，一个表示法，合起来指专门针对某一例的法。

items.en: Privus meant single, individual, or set apart, and it is the element that marks the word as being about one person rather than all.
items.cn: privus 意为单个的、个人的、被分出的，正是这个词里标记「针对一个人而非所有人」的成分。

items.en: Lex meant law or statute; joined to privus it produced privilegium, a statute made for or against a named individual.
items.cn: lex 意为法律、法令；与 privus 合起来造出 privilegium，即为某个指名的人制定、或针对他的法令。

items.en: In Roman law a privilegium was an exceptional measure concerning one person, city, or group, and later the word covered any special grant or exemption.
items.cn: 在罗马法中，privilegium 是针对某一个人、城市或群体的例外措施，后来泛指任何特别的授予或豁免。

items.en: Old French took the word as privilege, meaning a right or exemption granted by an authority, and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把它写作 privilege，指权威所授予的权利或豁免，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: English first used it for a right granted to a person, class, or town, and later added the softer sense of an honour one is glad to receive.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指授予个人、阶层或城市的权利，后来才添上「被人高看一眼、值得高兴的荣幸」这层较软的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin element privus and the English shapes built on the word; the near-meaning group gathers words for special rights and for honours.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁成分 privus 及由这个词长出的英语词形展开；近义组收表示特别权利与荣誉的词。

entries.definition: Having a special right or advantage, or having had a lucky opportunity.
entries.definitionCN: 享有特权或优势的，或有过幸运机会的。

entries.definition: Sharing a secret; it shares the Latin element privus but was built on privatus, so the formation differs.
entries.definitionCN: 参与秘密的；它同含拉丁成分 privus，却由 privatus 构成，所以构词方式不同。

entries.definition: Belonging to one person and kept from the public; it also goes back to privus through privatus.
entries.definitionCN: 属于个人、不公开的；它也经由 privatus 上溯到 privus。

entries.definition: To take something away from someone; built on the Latin verb privare, which shares the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 从某人那里拿走某物；建立在同词干的拉丁动词 privare 之上。

entries.definition: A condition that puts someone in a better position than others.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人处于比别人有利位置的条件。

entries.definition: Respect or a mark of respect that one is proud to receive.
entries.definitionCN: 值得自豪地接受的尊重或敬意。

entries.definition: A legal protection from prosecution or from a duty others must bear.
entries.definitionCN: 免于被起诉或免于承担他人义务的法律保护。

entries.definition: A right to something that a person believes they deserve.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人认为自己应得某项东西的权利。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin word for single to a Latin word for law, so a privilege is literally a law written for one.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语中表示单个的词与表示法律的词拼在一起，所以 privilege 字面上就是「为一个人写的法」。

normal.en: Privus means single and lex means law, so a privilegium was a bill aimed at one named person.
normal.cn: privus 意为单个，lex 意为法律，所以 privilegium 是针对某个指名者的法案。

normal.en: The -lege in privilege is the same Latin lex that appears in legal and legislature, all of them about law.
normal.cn: privilege 里的 -lege 就是 legal、legislature 里那个拉丁语 lex，都与法律有关。

normal.en: Privileged adds -ed and turns the special right into a description of the person who holds it.
normal.cn: privileged 加 -ed 后，把特别的权利变成持有这份权利的人的描述。

normal.en: Underprivileged puts under- in front of privileged: the people who sit below the line of normal advantage.
normal.cn: underprivileged 在 privileged 前加 under-：坐在正常优势线以下的那群人。

normal.en: The legal phrase privileged information keeps the old Roman idea of a wall around certain words.
normal.cn: 法律短语 privileged information 保留的正是罗马法那个老想法：在某些话周围砌一道墙。

abstract.en: A law for one person becomes a key for a few, and the same word then names both the key and the pleasure of being handed it.
abstract.cn: 一条为一个人立的法变成一把只配给少数人的钥匙，同一个词随后既指钥匙，也指接过钥匙时的那份高兴。

abstract.en: Privilege is advantage seen from the outside; from the inside it usually feels like an honour, which is why the word can be warm and cold at once.
abstract.cn: privilege 是从外面看的优势；从里面看，它常像一份荣誉，所以这个词能同时是暖的与冷的。

abstract.en: Every privilege marks a boundary: someone is inside the wall, and the word quietly says that someone else is not.
abstract.cn: 每一项特权都标出一道界：有人站在墙内，而这个词悄悄说明另一些人不在墙内。

examples.en: Only a few readers hold the privilege of working in that locked room.
examples.cn: 只有少数读者拥有在那间上锁的书库工作的特权。

examples.en: It was a privilege to hear the old pianist play one last time.
examples.cn: 能听这位老钢琴家最后一次演奏，是一种荣幸。

examples.en: Lawyers may claim privilege over what a client tells them.
examples.cn: 律师可以就当事人告知的内容主张保密特权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普里维利己」——只让自己人占的好处，就是 privilege。

root: 拉丁语 privus（单个的、个人的）+ lex（法律）→ privilegium（针对个人的法令、特免）→ 古法语 privilege → 中古英语 privilege。同族成分 privus 还生出 private、privy、deprive 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a right reserved for few; the senses divide into the right itself, the honour of receiving it, the legal shield in court, and the act of granting it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「只留给少数人的权利」；义项分成权利本身、得到它的荣幸、法庭上的保护盾，以及授予它的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pass card handed to only a few people at the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口只发给少数人的一张通行证。

branches.en: a brass key handed across a desk
branches.cn: 桌上递过来的一枚铜钥匙

branches.en: an audience of one with a great musician
branches.cn: 只为一个人响起的大师演奏

branches.en: a lawyer closing a folder before the court
branches.cn: 律师在法庭上合上文件夹

branches.en: a charter stamped for a single port
branches.cn: 只为一座港口盖章的特许状

branches.en: the same chosen feeling, legal and personal
branches.cn: 被选中的同一种感觉，一在法度，一在人心

intro.en: The word is two Latin pieces, a word for one and a word for law, plus French and English endings; the eight entries follow the seam between them.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个拉丁成分（一个表示一，一个表示法）加上法语与英语词尾构成；下面八条沿着这道接缝展开。

latinIntro.en: Both halves of the word are attested Latin, and the compound privilegium is recorded in Roman legal texts, so the cognates here need no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的两半都是有记录的拉丁语词，复合形式 privilegium 见于罗马法律文本，所以这里的同族词无需重构。

definition_zh: 恶意；怨恨；不顾；刁难
definition_en: a desire to hurt, annoy, or offend someone, or in spite of: without being affected by
core_image: 一只故意推倒积木塔的手：不为得到什么，只为看它倒下
scene: 游乐场角落，积木塔立得高高的。 The boy knocked over the tower out of pure spite.
sceneCN: 这里 spite 是「恶意」（第 1 个义项：故意伤人的心思）；句意为男孩纯粹出于恶意推倒了积木塔。图中可辨识物件：积木塔、游乐场、沙坑。

collocations.phrase: cut off one's nose to spite one's face

由 spiteful 加副词后缀构成，义为「恶毒地」
由 spiteful 加名词后缀构成，义为「恶毒；怨恨」
