senses.title: A desire to hurt or annoy
senses.definition: a desire to hurt, annoy, or offend another person, often without gain to oneself
senses.definitionCN: 想伤害、惹恼或冒犯他人之心，常于己无利
senses.example: He broke the window out of sheer spite.
senses.exampleCN: 他纯粹出于恶意打破了窗户。
senses.why: The hand pushes the tower not to build anything but to watch it fall.
senses.whyCN: 这只手推倒塔不是为建造什么，而是为看它倒塌。

senses.title: Ill will from a grudge
senses.definition: bitter ill will built up from past grievances
senses.definitionCN: 由旧怨积累的恶感
senses.example: She signed the letter out of old spite from their quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 她因争吵留下的旧怨带着恶意写了这封信。
senses.why: A wound that keeps hurting feeds its own small anger.
senses.whyCN: 持续作痛的伤口喂养着它自己的小小怒火。

senses.title: In spite of: despite
senses.definition: used before a fact that does not prevent the main statement, meaning despite
senses.definitionCN: 用于不阻止主句成立的事实之前，意为「尽管」
senses.example: In spite of the rain, the match went on.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，比赛照常进行。
senses.why: The obstacle stands in the sentence, yet the deed walks straight past it.
senses.whyCN: 句中立着障碍，行为却径直走过它。

senses.title: To annoy or thwart someone
senses.definition: to deliberately annoy or frustrate someone
senses.definitionCN: 蓄意惹恼或挫败某人
senses.example: The children spited each other with small tricks all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们整个下午用小恶作剧互相刁难。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: the push itself is given a name.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：推搡这个动作本身得了名字。

senses.title: Petty revenge in sayings
senses.definition: self-harming revenge, as in cut off your nose to spite your face
senses.definitionCN: 伤己式的报复，如「割鼻损面」之说
senses.example: Refusing the cheap ticket just to punish the airline was cutting off his nose to spite his face.
senses.exampleCN: 为惩罚航空公司而拒绝廉价机票，只是损人不成反害己。
senses.why: Old sayings warn that spite aimed at others often circles back home.
senses.whyCN: 古谚提醒：射向他人的恶意常绕回自己身上。

senses.title: Spite house or spite fence
senses.definition: a fence or building made purely to annoy neighbours
senses.definitionCN: 专为惹恼邻居而设的栅栏或建筑
senses.example: The tall spite fence went up the week after the quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵过后一周，那道赌气的高栅栏立了起来。
senses.why: Even walls and lumber can carry a grudge.
senses.whyCN: 连墙与木料都能承载一段怨恨。

senses.title: In spite of oneself
senses.titleCN: in spite of oneself：不由自主
senses.definition: although one did not intend or want to
senses.definitionCN: 虽非本意、非其所愿
senses.example: She laughed in spite of herself at the silly joke.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个傻笑话，她不由自主地笑了。
senses.why: The obstacle here is one's own intention, and the laughter slips past it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍是自己的本意，笑声却溜了过去。

senses.title: Archaic: contempt or scorn
senses.definition: contempt or scorn in older literary usage
senses.definitionCN: 旧文学用法中的轻蔑
senses.example: Old poems spoke of doing a thing in spite of the world.
senses.exampleCN: 旧诗中常说「不顾世人白眼而行某事」。
senses.why: The oldest face of the word is a raised chin against the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的面孔是朝人群昂起的下巴。

intro.en: Spite began as a Latin word for contempt and shortened on its way into English.
intro.cn: spite 原是拉丁语中表示「轻蔑」的词，进入英语的路上被截短了。

items.en: *spei- is generally reconstructed as "to point, sharp"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spei- 表示「指向、尖」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Latin despicere meant "to look down on", from de- "down" plus specere "to look".
items.cn: 拉丁语 despicere 意为「俯视、轻看」，由 de-「向下」加 specere「看」构成。

items.en: Old French despit meant "contempt, scorn", the noun of despiter "to look down on".
items.cn: 古法语 despit 意为「轻蔑」，来自动词 despiter「轻看」。

items.en: English took despite, and spite was cut from it in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语先收下 despite，十三世纪从中截出 spite。

items.en: The word now lives in malice and in the fixed phrase in spite of.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词既指恶意，也活在固定短语 in spite of 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of similar shape and the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers words for malice and defiance.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词与同一拉丁词族；近义组收表示恶意与违抗的词。

entries.definition: The fuller relative meaning despite; spite was cut from it.
entries.definitionCN: 更长的同族词，义为「尽管」，spite 即从它截出。

entries.definition: An adjective describing someone full of spite.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容满心恶意的人。

entries.definition: To eject saliva; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「吐唾沫」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: A place or location; merely sounds alike and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「地点、场所」；仅读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small fairy or a soft-drink brand; letters rearranged and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「小精灵」或某汽水品牌；字母换序，词源不同。

entries.definition: A stronger, colder wish to harm; spite is often pettier and hotter.
entries.definitionCN: 更强烈冷酷的伤害之心；spite 常更琐碎、更外露。

entries.definition: A lasting resentment held over time, often quiet.
entries.definitionCN: 长久怀有的怨恨，常不外露。

entries.definition: Bitter indignation at unfair treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 因不公对待而生的愤懑。

entries.definition: Open resistance; related to the despite line of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 公然违抗；与该词 despite 一脉相关。

entries.definition: The desire to get even for a wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 想为冤屈讨回公道的报复之心。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real phrase in spite of and the image of the deliberate push.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实短语 in spite of，以及「故意一推」的意象。

normal.en: despite is the tall brother: spite was clipped off the front of it.
normal.cn: despite 是高个子兄弟：spite 就是从它前面截下来的。

normal.en: Out of spite means the only reason was the wish to annoy.
normal.cn: out of spite 意为唯一的动机就是想惹恼人。

normal.en: In spite of the storm, the ship sailed: the storm could not stop it.
normal.cn: in spite of the storm，船照样起航：风暴拦不住它。

normal.en: The same Latin root specere "to look" gives despise: to look down on.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词根 specere「看」给出 despise「轻视」，即往下看。

normal.en: Cutting off your nose to spite your face warns against self-harming anger.
normal.cn: 「割鼻损面」警醒人们勿以害己的方式泄愤。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching not for a prize but for a tower to topple.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸出去不为取物，只为推倒一座塔。

abstract.en: In spite of is a wall in the sentence that the sentence walks around.
abstract.cn: in spite of 是句中的一面墙，而句子绕过了它。

abstract.en: A grudge kept warm long enough turns into spite: cold anger that pushes.
abstract.cn: 怨恨保温够久就变成 spite：会出手推人的冷怒。

examples.en: He hid her tools out of spite, not necessity.
examples.cn: 他藏起她的工具是出于恶意，并非必要。

examples.en: In spite of the traffic, they arrived before the ceremony began.
examples.cn: 尽管路上堵车，他们仍在仪式开始前赶到。

examples.en: The neighbours built a spite fence right along the property line.
examples.cn: 邻居们紧贴地界修了一道赌气栅栏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯派特」——不为好处只为看塔倒：恶意；不顾

root: spite 经古法语 despit「轻蔑」追溯至拉丁语 despicere「俯视」，由 de-「向下」加 specere「看」构成；一般认为印欧词根 *spei- 表示「指向、尖」，更早来源不确定。despite 与 despise 同属这一「往下看」词族。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spite run from the push of malice to the wall that gets walked past: hurting, grudging, defying, and outlasting.
sensesIntro.cn: spite 的义项从恶意的一推延展到被绕过的墙：伤人、怀怨、违抗与坚持。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that topples a tower only to watch it fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手推倒塔，只为看它倒塌。

branches.en: THE MALICE LINE: the push and the grudge that feeds it.
branches.cn: 恶意线：那一推，以及喂养它的旧怨。

branches.en: THE DESPITE LINE: the wall stands, the deed goes on anyway.
branches.cn: in spite of 线：墙立着，事照做。

branches.en: THE VERB LINE: the push itself gets a verb of its own.
branches.cn: 动词线：推搡动作自成动词。

branches.en: THE WARNING LINE: old sayings show spite turning on itself.
branches.cn: 警示线：古谚展示恶意反噬自身。

branches.en: THE BUILT GRUDGE LINE: fences carry spite, and old poems wear defiance.
branches.cn: 成形的怨恨线：栅栏承载恶意，旧诗披挂轻蔑。

intro.en: Spite was clipped from despite, and English builds on it with plain suffixes.
intro.cn: spite 由 despite 截短而来；英语用朴素后缀在其上构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin despicere and Old French despit are recorded; the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 despicere 与古法语 despit 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

items.example: The verb is the distant parent.

items.exampleCN: 这个名词给出英语 despite。

items.example: The short form split off in the thirteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 短形式于十三世纪分出。
它构成 despite 与 despise。

items.example: The seeing verb anchors the family.
It keeps the looking-down sense plainly.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「怀恶意的；恶毒的」
由 spiteful 加副词后缀构成，义为「恶毒地」
由 spiteful 加名词后缀构成，义为「恶毒；怨恨」
同源词，义为「尽管；不顾」

definition_zh: 哑的；说不出话的；沉默的；愚蠢的
definition_en: unable to speak, silent especially from shock, showing no words, or foolish in an informal sense
core_image: 一个人张着嘴，喉咙里却发不出任何声音
scene: 她站在门口，嘴唇动了动，却一个字也吐不出来。 He was struck dumb by the news.
sceneCN: 这里 dumb 是「一时说不出话的」（第 2 个义项：因震惊而语塞）；句意是那个消息让他一时说不出话来。

pos.zh: 形容词：哑的；说不出话的；沉默的；愚蠢的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「默默地；无言地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「哑；沉默」
由本词与 bell 复合，义为「哑铃」

senses.title: Unable to speak
senses.definition: physically unable to speak, either from birth or because of illness or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因先天原因或疾病、受伤而在生理上无法说话
senses.example: The illness left him dumb for almost a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那场病让他将近一年说不出话。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the body cannot produce speech, and the word names the absence of voice itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：身体无法发出言语，这个词直接命名了声音的缺席。

senses.title: Silent from shock
senses.definition: temporarily unable to speak because of strong emotion, especially shock or fear
senses.definitionCN: 因强烈情绪尤其是震惊或恐惧而一时说不出话
senses.example: He was struck dumb by the news.
senses.exampleCN: 那个消息让他一时说不出话来。
senses.why: The body is fine, but emotion takes the voice away for a moment; the same adjective covers a temporary silence.
senses.whyCN: 身体没毛病，是情绪一时夺走了声音；同一个形容词覆盖了这种暂时的沉默。

senses.title: Foolish, in informal use
senses.definition: foolish or stupid, used informally and often lightheartedly
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢的、犯傻的，属口语用法，常带轻松口气
senses.example: It was a dumb question, but nobody laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个傻问题，但没人笑。
senses.why: Speechlessness and slowness of mind were once linked, so the old word for mute slid into informal use for foolish.
senses.whyCN: 说不出话与头脑迟缓曾被联系在一起，于是这个表示「哑」的旧词滑入了口语的「愚蠢」。

senses.title: Without words
senses.definition: performed or expressed without speech, as in a dumb show or dumb waiter
senses.definitionCN: 不用言语来表演或表达的，如哑剧或无声传菜架
senses.example: The actors told the whole story in a dumb show.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们用一出哑剧讲完了整个故事。
senses.why: Anything that works without speech can be called dumb, from a silent performance to a mechanical lift.
senses.whyCN: 任何不靠言语运作的东西都可以叫 dumb，从无声的表演到机械升降架。

intro.en: Dumb is an Old English adjective shared across the Germanic languages, and its sense widened from mute to silent and then to foolish.
intro.cn: dumb 是古英语形容词，为多种日耳曼语言共有，其词义从「哑」扩展到「沉默」，再扩展到「愚蠢」。

items.en: A root connected with being mute or confused is sometimes reconstructed, but its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 有时会重构出一个与「哑、茫然」相关的词根，但其确切形式不确定。

items.en: The Germanic adjective is reconstructed as dumbaz, meaning unable to speak.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的这个形容词被重构为 dumbaz，意为「不能说话的」。

items.en: Old English dumb meant mute, and it could already describe animals without human speech.
items.cn: 古英语 dumb 意为「哑的」，当时已可形容不会说人话的动物。

items.en: The sense widened from permanent muteness to any silence, including silence caused by emotion.
items.cn: 词义从永久性失语扩展到任何沉默，包括情绪造成的沉默。

items.en: The informal sense of foolish is recorded later; it grew from the older link between speechlessness and slowness.
items.cn: 口语中「愚蠢」的义项记录较晚，是从「说不出话」与「迟钝」的旧有关联发展来的。

items.en: Dumb luck, dumb show and dumbbell keep the old word alive in fixed expressions and compounds.
items.cn: dumb luck、dumb show 与 dumbbell 让这个旧词在固定表达和复合词里继续活着。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dumb; the near-meaning group separates mute, silent and speechless by cause and duration.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dumb 构成的词形；近义组按原因与持续时间区分 mute、silent 与 speechless。

entries.definition: In a silent or speechless way; dumb plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「默默地、无言地」，由 dumb 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to speak or of being silent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指不能说话或沉默的状态。

entries.definition: A short bar with weights at each end; dumb plus bell, with a different sense of dumb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「哑铃」，由 dumb 与 bell 复合，此处 dumb 取另一层含义。

entries.definition: Completely astonished and unable to speak; dumb plus the old verb found.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「目瞪口呆的」，由 dumb 与旧动词 found 复合。

entries.definition: Unable to speak, often by birth or injury; more clinical and neutral than dumb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「哑的」，常指先天或受伤所致，比 dumb 更临床、更中性。

entries.definition: Making no sound; it describes the absence of noise rather than the ability to speak.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「沉默的、无声的」，描述没有声音，而非说话能力。

entries.definition: Unable to speak for a moment, usually from strong emotion; close to the shock sense of dumb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「说不出话的」，通常因强烈情绪而起，接近 dumb 的震惊义。

entries.definition: Without a voice, literally or figuratively; often used for groups without power to speak.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无声的、失声的」，也常指没有发言权的群体。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the physical loss of voice and then follow the word into shock, jokes and silent performance.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从生理上失去声音出发，再跟着这个词走进震惊、玩笑和无声表演。

normal.en: Dumb first means the voice cannot come out at all.
normal.cn: dumb 最初指声音根本发不出来。

normal.en: Shock can make a speaking person dumb for a moment.
normal.cn: 震惊能让一个会说话的人一时变哑。

normal.en: Struck dumb is the fixed phrase for being silenced by surprise.
normal.cn: struck dumb 是被惊讶得说不出话的固定说法。

normal.en: Dumb luck is luck with no cleverness behind it.
normal.cn: dumb luck 是背后没有半点聪明的运气。

normal.en: A dumb show tells a story with no words at all.
normal.cn: dumb show 完全不用语言来讲故事。

abstract.en: Picture an open mouth with a small locked door where the voice should come out.
abstract.cn: 想象一张张开的嘴，声音本该出来的地方却是一扇锁住的小门。

abstract.en: The same locked door appears for a moment on a shocked face, then opens again.
abstract.cn: 同一扇锁住的门在一张震惊的脸上短暂出现，然后又打开。

abstract.en: Dumb is about a missing voice, and every sense removes it in a different way.
abstract.cn: dumb 讲的是缺失的声音，每个义项都以不同方式拿走了它。

examples.en: He was struck dumb by the news.
examples.cn: 那个消息让他一时说不出话来。

examples.en: It was a dumb question, but nobody laughed.
examples.cn: 那是个傻问题，但没人笑。

examples.en: She stared at him, dumb with anger.
examples.cn: 她盯着他，气得说不出话。

dict_mnemonic.text: dumb 是一张嘴却发不出声：生理上是哑，情绪上是惊得说不出话，口语里就成了「犯傻」。

root: 古英语 dumb「哑的」，为日耳曼语共有词，重构形式作 dumbaz；中古英语起从永久失语扩展到任何沉默，十九世纪又发展出口语「愚蠢」义。更早的印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of dumb all describe a missing voice: a body that cannot speak, a person silenced by shock, a mind that seems to have no words, and a performance done without speech.
sensesIntro.cn: dumb 的四个义项都在描述缺席的声音：不能说话的身体、被震惊夺去声音的人、似乎没有言语的头脑，以及不用语言的表演。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open mouth with no sound coming out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张张开的嘴，却发不出任何声音。

branches.en: THE BODY: the voice is physically absent, whether from birth or from illness.
branches.cn: 身体线：声音在生理上缺席，无论先天还是疾病所致。

branches.en: THE EMOTION: shock or fear takes the voice away for a moment.
branches.cn: 情绪线：震惊或恐惧一时夺走了声音。

branches.en: THE JOKE: the old silence slides into informal talk about foolishness.
branches.cn: 玩笑线：古老的沉默滑入口语里关于「犯傻」的说法。

branches.en: THE STAGE: a story told with gestures and no words at all.
branches.cn: 舞台线：只用手势、完全不用语言讲的故事。

branches.en: ONE ABSENCE: whether permanent, temporary or staged, the voice is what is missing.
branches.cn: 同一种缺席：无论永久、暂时还是表演性的，缺的都是声音。

intro.en: Dumb is a native Germanic adjective; English adds -ly, -ness, -er, -est and compounds such as dumbbell.
intro.cn: dumb 是本族语日耳曼语形容词；英语加 -ly、-ness、-er、-est，并构成 dumbbell 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; Latin mutus, mute, is a semantic counterpart only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 mutus（哑的）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The adjective is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是词族的基础。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「默默地；无言地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「哑；沉默」
由本词与 bell 复合，义为「哑铃」

definition_zh: 令人愉快的；有乐趣的
definition_en: giving pleasure and making you feel happy
core_image: 一场让人从头笑到尾的聚会，散场时大家还在门口聊天
scene: 周末的午后，一群孩子在草地上追着风筝跑，笑声不断。 It was an enjoyable afternoon for everyone in the park.
sceneCN: 这里 enjoyable 是「令人愉快的」（第 1 个义项：能带来快乐的）；句意：对公园里的每个人来说，这都是一个愉快的下午。

derivatives.zh: 享受；喜爱
享受；乐趣
愉快地

senses.title: Giving pleasure
senses.definition: making you feel happy and interested
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到快乐并投入其中
senses.example: It was an enjoyable evening with old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个和老朋友共度的愉快夜晚。
senses.why: The -able ending means able to give, so enjoyable describes something that gives enjoyment.
senses.whyCN: -able 词尾表示「能够给予」，所以 enjoyable 描述「能带来享受的事物」。

senses.title: Pleasant rather than exciting
senses.definition: pleasant and easy to like, without being very intense
senses.definitionCN: 令人舒服、容易喜欢，但不算特别激烈
senses.example: The book is enjoyable but not very deep.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书读起来轻松愉快，但不算深刻。
senses.why: Enjoyment can be quiet as well as intense, so the adjective covers mild pleasantness too.
senses.whyCN: 享受可以安静也可以强烈，所以这个形容词也涵盖温和的愉悦。

intro.en: Enjoyable is enjoy plus the ending -able, meaning able to give enjoyment.
intro.cn: enjoyable 是 enjoy 加词尾 -able，意为「能够带来享受的」。

items.en: Gaudere means to rejoice and lies behind the joy in enjoy.
items.cn: gaudere 意为欢欣，是 enjoy 中 joy 的来源。

items.en: Enjoir means to take pleasure in something.
items.cn: enjoir 意为从某物中获得快乐。

items.en: Middle English enjoy names the act of taking pleasure.
items.cn: 中古英语 enjoy 指获得快乐的动作。

items.en: English adds -able to form enjoyable, able to give pleasure.
items.cn: 英语加 -able 构成 enjoyable，意为「能带来快乐的」。

items.en: The word spreads in reviews and travel writing as a mild praise.
items.cn: 这个词在评论和游记中传播，用作温和的赞美。

items.en: Modern English uses it for experiences that are pleasant and satisfying.
items.cn: 现代英语用它描述愉快而令人满足的经历。

note.en: Enjoyable is the adjective of enjoy, and it sits near pleasant and entertaining words without their stronger claims.
note.cn: enjoyable 是 enjoy 的形容词，与 pleasant、entertaining 等词相邻，但语气更温和。

entries.definition: to take pleasure in something
entries.definitionCN: 享受；喜爱

entries.definition: pleasure gained from something
entries.definitionCN: 享受；乐趣

entries.definition: in a pleasant way
entries.definitionCN: 愉快地

entries.definition: giving a mild feeling of pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；宜人的

entries.definition: very pleasant indeed
entries.definitionCN: 令人非常愉快的

entries.definition: enjoyable and amusing
entries.definitionCN: 有趣的；好玩的

entries.definition: interesting and amusing to watch or read
entries.definitionCN: 有娱乐性的

normalIntro.en: Enjoyable is just enjoy plus -able, so anything that can be enjoyed is enjoyable.
normalIntro.cn: enjoyable 就是 enjoy 加 -able，所以任何能被享受的东西都是 enjoyable。

normal.en: Take enjoy, add -able: able to give joy.
normal.cn: 取 enjoy 加 -able：能够带来快乐。

normal.en: An enjoyable experience is one you would gladly repeat.
normal.cn: an enjoyable experience 是一段你愿意再经历一次的经历。

normal.en: The ending -ably turns it into the adverb enjoyably.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ably 把它变成副词 enjoyably。

normal.en: Compare enjoyable and delighted: one gives pleasure, one feels it.
normal.cn: 对比 enjoyable 与 delighted：一个给予快乐，一个感受快乐。

normal.en: Highly enjoyable is a common way to praise a book or show.
normal.cn: highly enjoyable 是赞美书或演出的常用说法。

abstract.en: Picture a picnic where nobody wants to pack up.
abstract.cn: 想象一次野餐，谁也不想收拾离开。

abstract.en: Imagine a film that makes the whole row laugh at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一部让整排观众同时发笑的电影。

abstract.en: Think of a walk with no destination but good company.
abstract.cn: 想象一次没有目的地、只有好同伴的散步。

examples.en: We had an enjoyable afternoon by the lake.
examples.cn: 我们在湖边度过了一个愉快的下午。

examples.en: The class is both enjoyable and useful.
examples.cn: 这门课既有趣又有用。

examples.en: She found the work surprisingly enjoyable.
examples.cn: 她发现这份工作出乎意料地令人愉快。

dict_mnemonic.text: enjoy（享受）+ -able（能……的）＝能带来享受的，即令人愉快的；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: enjoy（享受，源自拉丁语 gaudere「欢欣」）+ 形容词词尾 -able，表示「能够带来快乐的」。

sensesIntro.en: Something that gives pleasure is the basic sense, and milder pleasantness is its quieter extension.
sensesIntro.cn: 能带来快乐是基本义，而较温和的愉悦是它更安静的延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an experience people would happily repeat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段人们愿意再来一次的经历。

branches.en: Giving pleasure is the direct meaning of the -able form.
branches.cn: 带来快乐，是 -able 形式的直接含义。

branches.en: Mild pleasantness is a quieter degree of the same pleasure.
branches.cn: 温和的愉悦，是同样快乐中更轻的程度。

branches.en: Both strong fun and quiet comfort count as enjoyable.
branches.cn: 热闹的乐趣与安静的舒适都算 enjoyable。

branches.en: The adjective describes the experience, not the person feeling it.
branches.cn: 这个形容词描述经历本身，而不是感受它的人。

branches.en: It often appears as modest praise rather than high excitement.
branches.cn: 它常作为温和赞美出现，而不是高度兴奋。

intro.en: Enjoyable is a transparent English adjective: enjoy plus -able.
intro.cn: enjoyable 是构词透明的英语形容词：enjoy 加 -able。

latinIntro.en: The base enjoy goes back to Latin gaudere, to rejoice, and -able means able to give.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 enjoy 可上溯到拉丁语 gaudere（欢欣），-able 表示「能够给予」。

items.example: Enjoy is the base of enjoyable.
items.exampleCN: enjoy 是 enjoyable 的基础词。
enjoyable 由 enjoy 与 -able 合成。
enjoyment 共享 enjoy 词干。

items.example: Gaudere is the distant root of enjoy.
items.exampleCN: gaudere 是 enjoy 的远源。

items.example: En- opens the base verb enjoy.
items.exampleCN: en- 出现在基础动词 enjoy 开头。

definition_zh: 面板；镶板；控制面板；专家小组；陪审团名单；（漫画）分格；固定样本组
definition_en: a flat rectangular piece fitted into a frame or surface; also a group of people selected to sit together and give opinions or make decisions
core_image: 一块绷在框架里的方形板，也可以是一群人选出来坐到同一张长桌后面
scene: 演播室里，四位专家坐在长桌后。 A square panel of lights came on above the table, and the host asked the four experts beneath it to begin.
sceneCN: 这里 panel 是「嵌在框架里的平板、灯板」（第 1 个义项：嵌在框架里的平板）；句意：长桌上方一块方形灯板亮起，主持人请坐在它下面的四位专家开始讨论。图中可辨识物件：长桌、四把椅子、专家名牌、方形灯板、麦克风；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: （选出的）专家小组；评审团；讨论组

forms.label: 过去式／过去分词（英式拼写）
过去式／过去分词（美式拼写）

derivatives.zh: 小组成员；评审之一
镶板材料；镶板工程（美式拼写）
装有镶板的（英式拼写）
分面板；子面板；下级小组
小组讨论（复合名词）

senses.title: A flat piece fitted into a frame
senses.definition: a usually rectangular piece of wood, glass, or metal that forms part of a surface or is set into a frame
senses.definitionCN: 通常为矩形的木、玻璃或金属板，构成某个表面的一部分，或嵌在框架里
senses.example: One panel of the door was cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 门上有一块镶板裂了。
senses.why: The word began as the name of a square piece of cloth. A piece cut to fit a frame keeps that shape, so the first modern sense is simply a flat rectangle inserted into a larger surface.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一块方形的布。裁好嵌进框架的一块仍保留那个形状，因此最早的现代义就是“插进更大表面里的一块平板”。

senses.title: The surface you operate: control panel
senses.titleCN: 你操作的那块面：控制面板
senses.definition: a flat surface on a machine or device that holds the controls, dials, or screens
senses.definitionCN: 机器或装置上集中安放控制键、旋钮或屏幕的平面
senses.example: The pilot checked the panel before takeoff.
senses.exampleCN: 起飞前飞行员检查了仪表板。
senses.why: A fitted board is a natural place to mount switches. Once the board carries the controls, the object becomes the interface, and the panel is what the hand reaches for.
senses.whyCN: 嵌装好的板面天然适合安装开关。一旦这块板承载了控制装置，它就成了人机接口，“面板”也就成了手要伸向的那块地方。

senses.title: A selected group at one table
senses.titleCN: 被选出来坐在一起的一组人
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to discuss a subject, judge a competition, or advise on a matter
senses.definitionCN: 被选出来讨论某个议题、评审比赛或提供建议的一组人
senses.example: A panel of judges will review the entries.
senses.exampleCN: 一个评审小组将审阅参赛作品。
senses.why: The group sense grows from a written list of names: a panel was first the sheet on which chosen names were written. The paper gave its name to the people listed on it.
senses.whyCN: “一组人”的义项来自一张写有名字的名单：panel 最初指写着被选中者名字的那张纸。纸的名字后来转移到了纸上所列的人身上。

senses.title: The jury list, and the jury itself
senses.titleCN: 陪审员名单，以及陪审团
senses.definition: the list of people summoned to serve on a jury, or the jury so formed
senses.definitionCN: 被传唤担任陪审员者的名单，或由此组成的陪审团
senses.example: The clerk read the panel aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员在法庭上宣读了陪审员名单。
senses.why: In law the sheet of names came first: the panel was the roll. Then the word shifted to the body of people on the roll, which is the same paper-to-people transfer seen in the expert sense.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，先有那张名单：panel 是名册。随后词义转到名册上的人，这与“专家组”义项中“纸→人”的转移完全相同。

senses.title: A frame in a comic strip
senses.definition: one framed picture or box in a comic strip or graphic novel
senses.definitionCN: 连环画或图像小说中被边框围住的一幅画或一格
senses.example: The final panel shows the empty street.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一格画的是空荡荡的街道。
senses.why: Each comic image is literally a rectangle drawn inside a border, a panel fitted into the page. The printing term for a bordered block transferred to the art form built out of such blocks.
senses.whyCN: 漫画的每一幅画就是画在边框里的一个矩形，即嵌进页面的一块板。印刷业对“带框区块”的叫法，转移到了由这种区块构成的画种上。

senses.title: A solar panel: a board that collects
senses.titleCN: 太阳能板：一块收集能量的板
senses.definition: one of the flat modules that make up a solar array, converting sunlight into electricity
senses.definitionCN: 组成太阳能阵列的平坦模块之一，把阳光转化为电能
senses.example: The roof holds twelve solar panels.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶装了十二块太阳能板。
senses.why: The object is again a flat rectangle mounted into a frame, this time a roof or a rack. What changed is the function: the board no longer covers, it collects.
senses.whyCN: 这仍是嵌在框架（屋顶或支架）里的一块平板。改变的是功能：这块板不再用于遮盖，而是用于收集。

senses.title: A panel show: guests as a group
senses.titleCN: panel show：嘉宾作为一组出场
senses.definition: in broadcasting, a programme in which a group of guests discuss or compete
senses.definitionCN: 广播或电视中由一组嘉宾讨论或竞赛的节目
senses.example: The comedy panel show runs every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这档喜剧小组节目每周五播出。
senses.why: Television keeps the legal and expert group but changes the setting: the panel is now chosen for entertainment, and the group itself becomes the format of the programme.
senses.whyCN: 电视保留了法律与专家义里的“一组人”，却换了场景：panel 现在是为娱乐而挑选的，这一组人本身就成了节目的形式。

senses.title: A fixed sample followed over time
senses.titleCN: 长期追踪的固定样本组
senses.definition: in research, a group of the same people or households surveyed repeatedly over time
senses.definitionCN: 研究中被反复调查、长期追踪的同一批人或家庭
senses.example: The household panel has been interviewed every year since 1990.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭样本组自 1990 年以来每年接受访谈。
senses.why: A panel here is a list that is deliberately kept closed: the same names stay on the roll so that changes can be measured. The legal roll of names becomes a scientific instrument.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 panel 是一份刻意保持封闭的名单：同一批名字始终留在名册上，以便测量变化。法律上的名册于是变成了科学工具。

intro.en: Panel is a small French word for a piece of cloth that grew into a word for boards, lists, and groups. The date of the Latin base is old, but its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: panel 本是法语里指一块布的小词，后来长成指板、名单与群体的词。其拉丁语基础年代久远，但更早来源不确定。

items.en: Panel is recorded meaning 'a piece of cloth, especially a square'. It comes from Old French panel, a diminutive of pan 'piece of cloth'.
items.cn: panel 最早记录于 14 世纪早期，意为“一块布，尤指方形的布”。它来自古法语 panel，是 pan“一块布”的指小形式。

items.en: The legal sense appears: the panel is the schedule or roll of jurors. The sheet of paper is named first; the jury named on it follows later.
items.cn: 法律义出现：panel 指陪审员的名单或名册。先命名那张纸，纸上所列的陪审团随后才被这样称呼。

items.en: The sense 'group of experts' is recorded, again by transfer from a list of selected names to the people themselves.
items.cn: “专家组”义记录于 16 世纪 70 年代，同样是“被选中者的名单”转移到“这些人本身”。

items.en: The wooden architectural sense becomes common: a panel is a board set into wainscot or a door. The verb appears in the 15c. as empanel 'to enter on a roll' and in the 1630s as 'to fit with panels'.
items.cn: 建筑木作义在 1600 年前后普及：panel 是嵌进护墙板或门里的木板。动词 15 世纪出现，作 empanel“列入名册”；17 世纪 30 年代又有“装镶板”义。

items.en: Technology multiplies the board: control panel, instrument panel, solar panel. Media adds the comic panel and the panel show; social science adds the survey panel.
items.cn: 技术让“板”大量增殖：控制面板、仪表板、太阳能板。传媒加上漫画分格与小组节目；社会科学加上调查样本组。

note.en: The first group separates near spellings; the second compares words for organised groups of people.
note.cn: 第一组把形近词分开；第二组比较表示“有组织的一组人”的词。

entries.definition: relating to punishment, especially under the law. One letter differs, and its root is poena 'penalty', not pannus 'cloth'.
entries.definitionCN: 与刑罚有关的，尤指法律上的。只差一个字母，其词根是 poena“惩罚”，不是 pannus“布”。

entries.definition: sudden uncontrolled fear. It looks close but comes from Pan, the Greek god whose sudden appearances caused alarm.
entries.definitionCN: 突如其来的失控恐惧。外形相近，但来自希腊神 Pan——他的突然出现会引发惊惶。

entries.definition: the boards that line a wall, or the work of fitting them. It is the noun from panel, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 墙面上的镶板，或安装镶板的工程。它是 panel 派生的名词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: a member of a panel. The -ist suffix marks a person, so it is a true derivative.
entries.definitionCN: 小组或评审组的一员。-ist 后缀标记人，因此它是真正的派生词。

entries.definition: a formally appointed group that meets to decide or manage. It has authority and procedure; a panel is often advisory or judging.
entries.definitionCN: 正式任命、开会决策或管理的团体。它有权力与程序；panel 常是咨询性或评审性的。

entries.definition: the group of people who decide a case in court. A panel can be the list from which the jury is drawn.
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上裁决案件的一组人。panel 可以指从中抽取陪审员的那份名单。

entries.definition: the group that governs a company or institution. It is permanent and powerful, while a panel is usually assembled for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 治理公司或机构的团体。它是常设且有实权的，而 panel 通常为某项任务临时组成。

entries.definition: a meeting or place for open discussion, often with an audience. It stresses exchange; a panel stresses the few selected speakers.
entries.definitionCN: 公开讨论的会议或场所，常有听众。它强调交流；panel 强调被选出的少数发言者。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the board and the table, then three abstract images about selection and framing.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕“板”和“长桌”的挂钩，再用三个关于“遴选与取景”的抽象画面。

normal.en: panel and pane: a window pane is a sheet of glass, and a panel is a sheet fitted into a frame. Same shape, same idea.
normal.cn: panel 与 pane：窗玻璃是一整片，panel 是嵌进框架的一片。形状相同，想法也相同。

normal.en: A control panel is where your fingers walk: buttons arranged on one flat board.
normal.cn: 控制面板是手指行走的地方：按钮排在同一块平板上。

normal.en: Think of a talk show: four chairs behind one long desk. The desk makes the group a panel.
normal.cn: 想一场脱口秀：一张长桌后四把椅子。那张长桌把这一组人变成 panel。

normal.en: A jury panel is first a list on paper, then the people on the paper. Paper first, people second.
normal.cn: 陪审团 panel 先是纸上的一份名单，然后才是名单上的人。先纸，后人。

normal.en: Solar panels are panels that stopped covering walls and started collecting light.
normal.cn: 太阳能板是不再盖墙、改去收集光的面板。

abstract.en: A panel is a frame that decides what counts: the board cuts a piece out of a larger surface and makes it the unit.
abstract.cn: panel 是一个决定“什么算数”的框：它从更大的表面里切出一块，让这块成为单位。

abstract.en: A panel of people is a list made visible: selection is the real subject, and the table is only where the list sits.
abstract.cn: 由人组成的 panel 是一份被看见的名单：真正的主角是“遴选”，长桌只是名单落座的地方。

abstract.en: Every panel hides the rest of the wall. What is outside the frame is as important as what is inside.
abstract.cn: 每一块面板都遮住了墙的其余部分。框外之物与框内之物同样重要。

examples.en: The inspector opened the control panel and found a loose wire.
examples.cn: 检查员打开控制面板，发现一根松动的电线。

examples.en: A panel of three teachers will interview the candidates.
examples.cn: 一个由三位教师组成的小组将面试候选人。

examples.en: The survey follows the same panel of families for ten years.
examples.cn: 这项调查对同一批家庭样本追踪十年。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 pan 记成“一片”，-el 记成“小块”：一片裁好的方板；一群被写进同一张名单的人，也像排在同一块板上。
dict_mnemonic.text: pan（一片布、一片） + -el（指小）→ 嵌板、面板 → 名单 → 坐在名单上的一组人

root: 古法语 panel（一块布）< 通俗拉丁 *pannellus < 拉丁 pannus“布片”；pannus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one object and one list: a fitted square of cloth or wood becomes a control surface, a comic frame, and a solar module; meanwhile a roll of selected names becomes a jury, an expert group, a broadcast format, and a research sample.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项沿着“一块板”和“一份名单”两条线展开：裁好嵌进去的方板变成控制面、漫画格与太阳能模块；而被选中者的名册则变成陪审团、专家组、节目形式与研究样本。

core.en: A square board set into a frame, and a sheet of names laid on a table
core.cn: 一块嵌进框架的方形板，以及一张铺在桌上的名单

branches.en: The board and its working face: a fitted rectangle becomes the place where controls sit.
branches.cn: 板与它的工作面：一块嵌好的矩形变成安放控制装置的地方。

branches.en: The selected group: experts at a table, then guests arranged as a programme format.
branches.cn: 被选出的一组：长桌后的专家，随后被编排成节目形式的嘉宾组。

branches.en: The roll of names: jurors summoned by a list, and a sample kept on a list for years.
branches.cn: 名册：按名单传唤的陪审员，以及多年保留在同一名单上的样本。

branches.en: The framed rectangle as an artistic unit: one bordered picture in a comic strip.
branches.cn: 作为艺术单位的带框矩形：连环画中被边框围住的一格。

branches.en: A board that collects: a solar panel turning sunlight into current.
branches.cn: 一块收集能量的板：把阳光变成电流的太阳能板。

intro.en: Panel has a small but clear family: the base word, its person noun, its material noun, and a few prefixed or compound forms.
intro.cn: panel 的词族不大但很清楚：基词、指人的名词、指材料的名词，以及几个加前缀或复合的形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is pannus 'cloth, rag', with a Vulgar Latin diminutive *pannellus. The further origin of pannus is uncertain, so no deeper root is asserted here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 pannus“布、破布”，其通俗拉丁语指小形式为 *pannellus。pannus 的更早来源不确定，因此这里不强行给出更深词根。

items.meaning: a piece of cloth; later a fitted board or a listed group
items.meaningCN: 一块布；后来指嵌板或名单上的一组人
items.example: The wall was divided into panels.
items.exampleCN: 墙面被分成一块块镶板。
每位小组成员有五分钟。

items.meaning: boards fitted to a wall; the work of fitting them
items.exampleCN: 橡木镶板覆盖了大厅墙面。

items.example: A panelled study faced the garden.
items.exampleCN: 一间镶板书房朝向花园。

items.meaning: a smaller panel within a larger one; a subordinate group
items.meaningCN: 大面板中的分面板；下级小组
items.example: The subpanel reports to the main committee.
items.exampleCN: 下级小组向主委员会汇报。

items.meaning: to enter a person on a jury roll; to form a panel
items.meaningCN: 把某人列入陪审员名册；组成小组
items.exampleCN: 法庭组成了十二人的陪审团。

items.meaning: a piece of cloth (the source of panel)
items.example: Pan in Old French meant a patch of cloth.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 pan 指一块布片。

items.meaning: a single sheet of glass in a frame
items.example: The ball broke a pane of the window.
items.exampleCN: 球打碎了窗户的一块玻璃。

items.meaning: a research design that re-surveys the same sample
items.meaningCN: 对同一样本重复调查的研究设计
items.example: The panel study tracked income for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 该样本研究追踪收入达十年。

latinEntries.meaning: cloth, rag, a piece of fabric
latinEntries.example: Pannus is the base of French pan and English panel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pannus 是法语 pan 与英语 panel 的基础词。

latinEntries.meaning: a small piece of cloth (reconstructed Vulgar Latin)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一小块布（重构的通俗拉丁语形式）
latinEntries.example: Vulgar Latin *pannellus led to Old French panel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 通俗拉丁语 *pannellus 演变为古法语 panel。

definition_zh: 戏剧的；戏剧性的；显著的；夸张的
definition_en: relating to drama, or sudden, striking, and full of strong feeling
core_image: 门被推开的一瞬，所有目光都转过去
scene: 会场忽然安静，灯光一转，演讲者从侧门大步走上台。 The announcement had a dramatic effect on the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 dramatic 是「显著的、戏剧性的」（第 2 个义项）；句意是这项宣布对人群产生了显著的影响。

pos.zh: 形容词：戏剧的；戏剧性的；显著的；夸张的

derivatives.zh: 由 dramatic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「大幅度地；戏剧性地」
由 dramatic 加 -s 构成，义为「戏剧表演；夸张做作」

senses.title: Relating to plays and acting
senses.definition: connected with plays, acting, or the theatre
senses.definitionCN: 与戏剧、表演或剧院有关的
senses.example: She joined a dramatic society at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学加入了一个戏剧社。
senses.why: The Greek noun drama named a staged action, and the ending -tic simply means belonging to it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语名词 drama 指被搬上舞台的行动，后缀 -tic 只表示「属于它」，所以这是最本分的义项。

senses.title: Sudden and very noticeable
senses.definition: large, sudden, and easy to notice, especially of a change or an effect
senses.definitionCN: 幅度大、来得突然、很容易被注意到，多形容变化或效果
senses.example: There has been a dramatic fall in prices.
senses.exampleCN: 价格出现了大幅下跌。
senses.why: A change that would look striking on stage is called dramatic, so the word came to mean strikingly large.
senses.whyCN: 一个在舞台上会显得触目惊心的变化，就被称作 dramatic，于是这个词有了「幅度惊人」的意思。

senses.title: Showy and full of strong feeling
senses.definition: expressing feelings in an exaggerated, theatrical way
senses.definitionCN: 以夸张、像演戏一样的方式表达情绪
senses.example: He let out a dramatic sigh and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他夸张地叹了口气，走出了房间。
senses.why: When ordinary behaviour copies stage acting, the same adjective describes it as overdone.
senses.whyCN: 当日常举动模仿舞台表演时，同一个形容词就用来形容它「演过头了」。

intro.en: Dramatic is Greek drama plus the adjective ending -tikos, filtered through Latin dramaticus and French dramatique.
intro.cn: dramatic 由希腊语 drama 加形容词词尾 -tikos 构成，经拉丁语 dramaticus 与法语 dramatique 传入英语。

items.en: Dran meant to do or act, and drama was the deed performed.
items.cn: dran 意为「做、行动」，drama 是被做出来的事。

items.en: The adjective meant skilled in acting or belonging to drama.
items.cn: 这个形容词表示「擅长表演的」或「属于戏剧的」。

items.en: Latin kept the adjective for anything connected with plays.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留这个形容词，指与戏剧有关的事物。

items.en: French carried the form toward modern spelling and meaning.
items.cn: 法语把这个形式推向近代拼写与含义。

items.en: English adopted dramatic for stage matters and soon extended it to striking events.
items.cn: 英语采用 dramatic 指舞台事务，很快又扩展到惊人的事件。

items.en: The word now covers theatre, big changes, and exaggerated behaviour.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖戏剧、巨大变化与夸张举止三方面。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same family; the near-meaning group compares three words for striking change.
note.cn: 形近组同属一个词族；近义组比较三个表示「变化惊人」的词。

entries.definition: A play, or the art of performing plays.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「戏剧」，是 dramatic 的基础词。

entries.definition: In a striking way, or by a large amount.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大幅度地；戏剧性地」，由 dramatic 加 -ally 构成。

entries.definition: To adapt for the stage or to exaggerate.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改编成剧；夸大」，与 dramatic 同族。

entries.definition: Very noticeable and impressive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引人注目的」，强调视觉冲击。

entries.definition: Sudden and large, especially of a change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「急剧的」，多修饰变化的幅度。

entries.definition: Exaggerated in manner, like an actor on stage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「夸张做作的」，偏贬义，接近 dramatic 的第三个义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the stage picture from real theatre to big changes to overacting.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着舞台画面，从真正的戏剧走到巨大变化，再到演过头。

normal.en: Drama plus -tic simply means of the stage.
normal.cn: drama 加 -tic 就是「属于舞台的」。

normal.en: A dramatic rise is a change big enough to look like a scene.
normal.cn: dramatic rise 就是大到像一场戏的变化。

normal.en: Dramatic irony is the audience knowing what the character does not.
normal.cn: dramatic irony 指观众知道而剧中人不知道。

normal.en: A dramatic sigh is acting without a stage.
normal.cn: dramatic sigh 就是没有舞台的表演。

normal.en: Dramatics as a plural noun means either amateur theatre or showy behaviour.
normal.cn: 复数名词 dramatics 既指业余戏剧，也指做作的举止。

abstract.en: Picture a door thrown open and every head turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被推开，所有脑袋同时转过去。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line dropping off the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线陡降，几乎掉出纸外。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to the forehead in mock despair.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按上额头，装作绝望。

examples.en: The city has seen dramatic growth in ten years.
examples.cn: 这座城市十年间出现了惊人的增长。

examples.en: Her dramatic reading held the whole room.
examples.cn: 她富有戏剧感的朗诵镇住了全场。

examples.en: He made a dramatic gesture with his coat and left.
examples.cn: 他夸张地甩了一下外套就走了。

dict_mnemonic.text: drama 是「戏」，-tic 是「……的」，所以 dramatic 是「像戏一样的」：既能指真的戏剧，也能指惊人的变化和夸张的举止。

root: 由希腊语 drama（行为、戏剧）加形容词词尾 -tikos 构成，经拉丁语 dramaticus 与法语 dramatique 进入英语。核心含义始终是「像舞台上那样引人注目」，因此兼指戏剧本身、巨大的变化与夸张的表达。

sensesIntro.en: From the stage the adjective moves to changes that look stage-worthy, then to people who act as if on stage.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从舞台出发，移向「像戏一样」的变化，再移向「仿佛在台上」的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door thrown open while every head turns.
core.cn: 核心意象：门被推开，所有目光同时转过去。

branches.en: THEATRE: the literal sense belongs to plays and acting.
branches.cn: 剧场线：字面义属于戏剧与表演，即第一个义项。

branches.en: SCALE: a change big enough to stage is described as dramatic.
branches.cn: 幅度线：大到可以搬上舞台的变化，被形容为 dramatic，即第二个义项。

branches.en: MANNER: behaviour that copies stage acting is called dramatic.
branches.cn: 举止线：模仿舞台表演的行为也叫 dramatic，即第三个义项。

branches.en: Real theatre and overacting share the same visible gestures.
branches.cn: 真正的戏剧与做作的举止，共享同一套夸张可见的手势。

branches.en: Both a dramatic fall and a dramatic sigh are meant to be noticed.
branches.cn: 大幅下跌与夸张的叹息，都是为了被人注意到。

intro.en: Dramatic is a Greek stem with a Greek adjective ending, reshaped by Latin and French.
intro.cn: dramatic 是希腊词干加希腊形容词词尾，再经拉丁语与法语改造的形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin dramaticus is recorded, and the Greek ending -tikos appears in Latin as -ticus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dramaticus 有文献记录，希腊词尾 -tikos 在拉丁语中作 -ticus。

items.exampleCN: drama 是 dramatic 的词干。
